questions.explanation: Completeness, uniqueness and validity describe properties of the data itself, and they are checked during preparation, well before any traffic is live.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these steps in the order a team follows when setting up drift monitoring for a deployed model.
options: Raise an alarm when a value falls outside its acceptable range
Capture live request and response samples from the endpoint
Compute reference statistics from the training data
Define the acceptable ranges the team is willing to live with
Schedule a periodic comparison of live samples against the reference
Retrain the model as soon as the endpoint receives its first request
questions.explanation: Monitoring needs something to capture, a reference to compare against, agreed ranges, a schedule, and only then an alarm; retraining on day one is not monitoring.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these steps in the order a team follows to tie a new model to the business outcome it is meant to improve.
options: Measure the candidate on held-out data against the target
Pick whichever model has the highest training score
State the business outcome the feature is meant to move
Set the target the candidate must reach on that metric
Confirm the business outcome moved after release
Choose a model metric that moves in step with that outcome
questions.explanation: Start from the business outcome, pick a model metric that tracks it, set the target, measure the candidate offline, and only then confirm that the business number actually moved.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Match each deployment technique to the purpose it serves.
prompts: Candidate sees live traffic while callers get the incumbent's answer
A small share of the new fleet serves traffic before the rest
Two full environments exist and traffic is switched between them
Capacity is added or removed as invocation volume changes
options: Auto scaling
Blue/green deployment
Shadow variant
Canary rollout
questions.explanation: A shadow copy never reaches callers, a canary moves a small share first, blue/green swaps whole environments, and auto scaling reacts to volume.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Match each production situation to the retraining approach it calls for.
prompts: Demand follows a seasonal pattern the team can predict in advance
Production performance fell below target and an alert fired
A candidate exists and must beat the incumbent on live traffic
Metrics hold at their reference level and no alert has fired
options: Challenger comparison before promotion
No retraining; the incumbent stays
Calendar-based scheduled retraining
Alarm-triggered retraining
questions.explanation: Known seasonality calls for a schedule, a monitoring alarm calls for triggered retraining, a ready candidate calls for a challenger comparison, and stable metrics call for no action.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A company runs a high-volume summarization workload on Amazon Bedrock and wants to understand what drives its bill. Which factor has the greatest direct effect on the cost of each request?
options: The number of concurrent applications sharing the account
The count of input tokens processed and output tokens generated
The size of the container image used to host the model
The number of developers with console access to the account
questions.explanation: On-demand foundation model pricing is metered per input and output token, so prompt length and generated length are the levers that move cost and latency together. Account activity, container size and developer counts do not change the token meter of a single invocation.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: During long conversations, a support agent bot gradually stops following its own operating instructions even though every request returns successfully. What best explains this behavior?
options: The tokenizer silently changed, so the same text now produces fewer tokens
A guardrail is blocking the instructions before they reach the model
The application is sending the requests to a different AWS Region
The context window is full, so the oldest tokens including the system prompt are evicted
questions.explanation: AWS describes the context window as a FIFO buffer: once it fills, each new token evicts the oldest one, and the system prompt is usually the oldest content. The call still succeeds, so behavior drifts instead of raising an error, a condition AWS calls context window overflow.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A developer wants agents built with different frameworks to reach the same external tools and data sources through one common standard. Which technology provides this?
options: Model Context Protocol
OAuth 2.0 authorization grants
OpenID Connect token exchange
Amazon S3 event notifications
questions.explanation: Model Context Protocol is the open standard that lets agents and AI applications connect to tools and data sources in a consistent way, and it is an explicit objective under agentic AI. OAuth, OpenID Connect and S3 notifications solve authentication and file events, not tool integration for agents.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is designing an agentic solution on AWS. Which capabilities are part of agentic AI as the exam defines it?
options: A supervisor agent that coordinates collaborator agents on a complex task
Managed memory that carries context across sessions for the same user
Runtime tool usage, where the model selects and invokes an API it needs
A guarantee that the agent will never produce an incorrect statement
Workflow orchestration in which the model decides the next step at runtime
Fixed, identical responses for every request without any reasoning steps
questions.explanation: Agentic AI covers multi-agent patterns, memory management, tool usage and workflow orchestration, which are the four capabilities listed here. Agents remain nondeterministic and fallible, so any option promising guaranteed correctness or fixed identical output is wrong.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Place these foundation model lifecycle stages in the order they occur.
options: Fine-tuning
Evaluation
Data selection
Pre-training
Model selection
questions.explanation: AWS defines the foundation model lifecycle as data selection, then model selection, then pre-training, fine-tuning and evaluation, with deployment and feedback following. Each stage builds on the previous one, so neither pre-training nor fine-tuning can start before the data and the model family are chosen.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Match each generative AI term to its definition.
options: Splitting a long document into smaller segments so each one fits a model's input limit
Designing and refining the instruction text sent to a model to improve its output
The unit of text a model reads and writes, produced by splitting input with a tokenizer
A generative model that creates new content by reversing progressively added noise
The maximum number of tokens a model can consider at one time
A dense numeric representation that places semantically similar items near each other
questions.explanation: A token is the model's unit of text, chunking splits long inputs into fitting segments, an embedding is a dense vector, the context window is the token budget for one call, prompt engineering is instruction design, and a diffusion model generates content by learning to reverse noise.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A marketing team wants a service that produces brand-new product illustrations from a written brief instead of retrieving existing artwork. Which generative AI use case does this represent?
options: Text-to-image generation
Sentiment analysis of customer reviews
Demand forecasting for inventory levels
Anomaly detection in payment records
questions.explanation: Image, video, and audio generation are the content-generation use cases the exam guide lists for generative AI models, typically implemented with a diffusion model behind a text-to-image API. The other three options are traditional ML tasks that label, forecast, or score existing records rather than create new content.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team asks why transformer-based language models handle long input sequences more effectively than recurrent networks. What is the best answer?
options: They store every training document verbatim and copy passages from memory
They reduce each input to a single fixed-size keyword before reading it
They read the sequence one position at a time and carry a hidden state forward
They process the whole sequence in parallel and let every token attend to every other token
questions.explanation: Transformers process the entire sequence in parallel using self-attention, which gives them faster training and the ability to handle much longer sequences than recurrent networks. Reading one position at a time with a hidden state describes the recurrent architecture that transformers replaced.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A support tool accepts a screenshot and a written question and returns a written answer. Which model type best describes this system?
options: A diffusion model that removes noise from an image over successive steps
An embedding model that returns only numeric vectors
A multi-modal model that accepts image and text input and produces text
A text-only large language model with a longer context window
questions.explanation: A multi-modal model accepts more than one input type, and the exam's modality table lists text-image-to-text models for exactly this shape. A diffusion model generates images, an embedding model returns vectors rather than answers, and a text-only model cannot read the screenshot.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: The exam guide describes the foundation model lifecycle as a cycle rather than a straight line. Which statement about that cycle is correct?
options: Feedback is gathered only before pre-training starts
Deployment is the final stage and no stage follows it
Evaluation happens once, before any fine-tuning is attempted
Feedback from the deployed model loops back into data selection for the next cycle
questions.explanation: The exam guide presents the foundation model lifecycle as a cycle of data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, and feedback, with feedback feeding back into data selection. Deployment is therefore a stage with a successor rather than an endpoint.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A ticket-classification prompt needs reliable output formatting on a simple task, and the team wants the smallest token increase that still controls the format. Which prompting approach fits?
options: Chain-of-thought instructions that ask the model to reason step by step
Few-shot prompting with three to five worked examples and the instruction placed at the end
Zero-shot prompting with an instruction and no examples at all
Self-consistency, sampling several reasoning paths and taking the majority answer
questions.explanation: AWS documents three to five examples as enough to control format on a simple classification task, with the instruction placed at the end of the prompt. Chain-of-thought and self-consistency add latency and output tokens that a simple formatting task does not need, and zero-shot gives the least format control.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team counts the tokens in the same policy document with two different Bedrock models and gets two different totals. What best explains the difference?
options: The two requests were billed at different token prices
Each model uses its own tokenizer, so the same text splits into different token sequences
One of the models silently discarded the middle of the document
Token counts differ only when the text contains characters outside the English alphabet
questions.explanation: Token counting is model-specific because different models use different tokenization strategies, which is why Bedrock exposes a CountTokens call that runs the selected model's tokenizer on the exact input. Pricing does not change counts, and no model truncates silently for a counting request.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A language model developer is reviewing what actually happens when a model reads text and compares meaning. Which statements are accurate?
options: Similarity between two embeddings is computed by the vector database rather than by the model
Chunking decides how much of a document reaches the model at once, which affects both token cost and relevance
A foundation model is adapted to new tasks through prompting or fine-tuning rather than retrained from scratch
Token counts always equal the number of words in the input text
The vector database creates the embeddings on demand, so no embedding model is involved
questions.explanation: An embedding model produces the vectors while the vector database performs the similarity search, chunking controls how much text enters the model and therefore both cost and relevance, and a foundation model is adapted through prompting or fine-tuning instead of retraining. Token counts do not match word counts, and embeddings come from an embedding model rather than from the database that stores them.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team's requests have become slow and expensive because every call carries the full policy manual, the entire chat history, and loosely related retrieval results. Which practices belong to context engineering?
options: Ranking retrieved passages and keeping only the most relevant ones
Budgeting tokens across the system prompt, the user input, the retrieved context, and the output
Summarizing older conversation turns instead of replaying them in full
Appending every retrieved document in full so that nothing is missed
Raising temperature so that the model explores a wider range of word choices
Setting the output token cap to the model maximum on every request
questions.explanation: Context engineering is the practice of deciding what enters the context window and what it costs, so re-ranking, token budgeting, and summarizing older turns all shrink the prompt while preserving relevance. Appending everything defeats that purpose, and temperature and output caps are generation settings rather than context selection.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Which changes reduce the token cost of an Amazon Bedrock workload without switching to a different model?
options: Setting the output token cap close to the typical answer length
Removing few-shot examples that add no measurable accuracy
Caching a long prefix that repeats across requests so it is not reprocessed each time
Sending only the top-ranked retrieved passages instead of the whole document
Adding chain-of-thought instructions to a simple routing task
Raising temperature to 1.0 so that responses are more varied
questions.explanation: Token-based pricing means cost follows input and output tokens, so tighter output caps, fewer unused examples, prefix caching, and leaner retrieved context all lower the bill for the same model. Chain-of-thought adds output tokens and latency, and temperature changes randomness rather than the number of tokens billed.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence the phases of one Amazon Bedrock agent invocation, from the incoming request to the streamed answer.
options: Post-processing formats the final answer, a phase that is off by default
Pre-processing validates the request and returns a validity rationale
The orchestration loop produces a rationale, predicts an action or knowledge-base query, and receives an observation
Answer chunks stream back to the calling application
The application installs a new foundation model into the agent's catalog
questions.explanation: AWS documents the runtime order as pre-processing, then the orchestration loop until an answer exists, then post-processing, which is disabled by default, and finally the streamed answer chunks. Installing models is a build-time concern and is not a runtime phase.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence one model-initiated tool call, from the outgoing request through to the final answer.
options: The model returns a tool-use stop reason together with a proposed JSON call
Your application executes the function and returns the result to the model
The model uses the result to produce the final natural-language answer
The model executes the function inside its own sandbox without your code
Your application sends the request with the tool definitions and their input schema
questions.explanation: With Converse tool configuration, your code supplies the tool schema, the model only proposes a JSON call, your application executes it, and the model turns the returned result into the answer. The model never executes the function itself, which is the boundary that defines raw tool use.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence one supervisor-based multi-agent interaction, from the customer question to the delivered answer.
options: The supervisor selects one collaborator agent for the request
The collaborator runs its action group and returns a result
The supervisor synthesizes the result into a single answer for the customer
The collaborator becomes the entry point for every future customer question
A customer question reaches the supervisor agent
questions.explanation: In supervisor with routing mode the supervisor stays the entry point, picks one collaborator, receives its result, and synthesizes the final answer for the customer. A collaborator never becomes the entry point, because clients always invoke the supervisor's alias.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each transformer concept, select the description that fits it.
options: What a token is searching for elsewhere in the sequence
Generating one token at a time, appending it, and running the model again
The label each token advertises about itself for attention scoring
Information injected so that the model knows the order in which tokens appear
The mechanism that lets every token weigh every other token in the sequence
questions.explanation: Self-attention scores every token against every other token using queries against keys, positional encoding supplies order because attention itself is permutation-invariant, and autoregressive decoding regenerates the sequence one token at a time.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each model concept, select the description that fits it.
options: A model that accepts more than one input type, such as an image plus a written question
An array of numbers produced by an embedding model and compared for similarity
A large model pre-trained on broad data and adaptable to many downstream tasks
AI that creates new text, image, audio, video, or code rather than only labeling data
A language model built from many stacked transformer blocks trained on broad corpora
questions.explanation: A foundation model is broad and adaptable, a multi-modal model takes several input types, a vector is the numeric output of an embedding model, a transformer-based large language model is a stacked-block architecture trained on broad text, and generative AI creates new content instead of only labeling data.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each generative AI use case, select the category it belongs to.
prompts: Drafting a condensed version of a long report
Creating a product illustration from a written brief
Translating a support article into another language
Answering customer questions in a chat window
options: Translation
Code generation
Summarization
AI assistant
Image generation
questions.explanation: These map directly onto the generative AI use cases the exam guide lists: summarization, image generation, translation, code generation, and AI assistants such as customer service agents. Each case produces new content rather than scoring or sorting existing records.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A design tool creates original images from written descriptions. Which generative technique underlies this kind of image generation?
options: Sequence-to-sequence translation of the input text
Clustering documents in embedding space
Diffusion models that iteratively denoise
A recurrent network that copies pixels from a reference image
questions.explanation: The exam guide names diffusion models as the technique behind image generation, where the model starts from noise and refines it step by step into an image.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A search feature must surface policy documents whose wording never contains the user's keywords but whose meaning matches the query. Which approach provides this?
options: Convert documents and queries into embedding vectors and search by vector similarity
Match exact keywords with a case-sensitive string comparison
Store the documents in a key-value store and look them up by document ID
Summarize every document into one sentence and compare text lengths
questions.explanation: Embeddings place semantically similar text near each other in vector space, so meaning-based retrieval works without keyword overlap; the guide pairs embeddings and vectors with exactly this role.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is splitting long documents into chunks before embedding them for retrieval. Which statements about chunking are correct?
options: Chunks that are too small can separate a sentence from the context it depends on
Overlap between neighboring chunks reduces the chance that a relevant passage is cut at a boundary
Chunk size influences how much supporting context each retrieved passage can supply to the model
Larger chunks always produce more accurate answers because they contain more words
Documents must be split exactly at sentence boundaries in every case
questions.explanation: Chunking trades context completeness against retrieval precision, and overlap protects boundaries; bigger is not automatically better and no single splitting rule fits every document.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Place the steps that turn raw text into contextual representations in the order they occur.
options: Process the sequence with attention layers to produce contextual representations
Break the text into tokens using the model's vocabulary
Train the model on the next-token objective
Look up a learned embedding vector for each token
Map each token to its integer ID in the vocabulary
questions.explanation: Tokenization precedes ID lookup, embeddings follow the IDs, and attention layers then build contextual representations; training the model is a separate earlier stage, not part of processing one input.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A semantic search embeds the user's question and asks the vector store to rank the most relevant policy passages. Which statement correctly describes how the store scores the results?
options: An exact keyword match on the query terms
A per-passage read where the foundation model scores each stored document
A token-count ranking that ignores word order
A geometric comparison such as cosine similarity between vectors
questions.explanation: Vector stores rank by geometric similarity between embedding vectors, commonly cosine similarity, so meaning matches even without shared keywords; keyword matching, token counting, or re-reading every passage with a model is not how retrieval scores results.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A tokenizer meets the invented product name Cloudifyx, which appears nowhere in its vocabulary, and represents it as several familiar character sequences instead of failing. Which behavior is this?
options: Subword tokenization, where rare words are split into known pieces
An out-of-vocabulary fallback that maps the word to a single unknown token
Chunking, where a document is split into passages that fit the model's input limit
Stop-sequence processing, where input is truncated at a configured marker
questions.explanation: Subword tokenizers keep frequent words whole and split rare or invented words into known pieces rather than replacing them with an unknown token; chunking and stop sequences act on longer text, not on individual words.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is choosing an embedding model for its retrieval pipeline. Which statements about embedding models are correct?
options: Vectors from two different embedding models are not directly comparable, so a corpus must be re-embedded if the model changes
Input longer than the model's documented text limit must be split before embedding
The model returns fixed-length numeric vectors rather than human-readable text
Embedding models rewrite and improve the source text before storing it
The vector database stores only the original wording and discards the numeric vectors
A larger cosine distance means the two texts are more semantically similar
questions.explanation: Embedding models emit fixed-size numeric vectors, reject input beyond their limits so long documents must be split, and are not interoperable across models; they do not rewrite text, the store keeps the vectors, and a larger cosine distance means less similarity.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A data scientist converts a vocabulary of 20,000 words into one-hot vectors and notices that every vector is mostly zeros with a single value of 1. Which representation should she use instead if she wants smaller vectors that also capture similarity?
options: Dense embeddings, where every dimension holds a learned continuous value
A bigger vocabulary that adds one more dimension for each new word
Character hashing, which maps each word to one fixed bucket index
N-gram counting, which keeps one active value but adds surrounding words
questions.explanation: Embeddings replace sparse one-hot tables with dense learned vectors, so semantically similar words sit close together and each vector is far smaller. Expanding the vocabulary or hashing characters still produces unrelated coordinates with no measure of similarity between them.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A retailer wants one search index that can answer both typed queries and uploaded photo queries over the same product catalog. Which property of multimodal embeddings makes a single index possible?
options: They turn every input into the same fixed-length token sequence before searching
They store images and text in separate vector spaces and merge the scores later
They map images and text into one shared vector space where related items sit close
They translate image pixels into words so only text-to-text search is needed
questions.explanation: Multimodal embedding models encode different modalities into a shared vector space, so a text query and an image query retrieve from the same index. Separate spaces would require two indexes and merged scores, and translating pixels to words would discard visual detail.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: While reviewing how self-attention works, an engineer asks which of the three projected vectors actually carries content into the next layer of the transformer.
options: The query vector, which states what this token is searching for
The value vector, which holds the content carried forward to the next layer
The key vector, which advertises what this token offers to the others
The positional vector, which records the token index in the sequence
questions.explanation: Attention scores are computed from queries matched against keys, and those scores are then used to weight the value vectors, so V is what passes onward. Queries and keys only drive the matching, while order is injected separately by positional encoding.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A support team is about to lower the temperature on its summarization endpoint because a review flagged rising spend and slow responses. Which variable actually drives both cost and latency for that endpoint?
options: The temperature value, which is metered for each degree of randomness
The batch size, which is always fixed at one request for a synchronous call
The model identifier, which costs the same no matter which model is used
The prompt and output tokens processed, which is the unit usage is metered in
questions.explanation: Model usage is metered and processed in tokens, so longer prompts and longer answers raise both the bill and the response time. Temperature changes sampling behavior only, and neither batch size nor the model name determines how much text was processed.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A developer sets the output token limit for a Converse request and wants the model to have as much room as possible to answer. How should that value be chosen?
options: Subtract the prompt tokens and a safety margin from the model context window
Set it equal to the full context window so every token is available to the model
Set it to a small fixed value so every response finishes quickly
Copy it from another model family, since the setting does not vary by model
questions.explanation: The prompt, the requested output, and a safety margin all draw from the same context window, so the output budget is the window minus prompt tokens minus margin. Matching the full window lets the request overflow and be rejected, while a small fixed value truncates answers that had room.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: An engineer sends a 560 by 560 pixel image to a vision model that bills image inputs as tokens. Using the documented image-sizing rule, roughly how many image tokens does that single picture count for?
options: About 100 tokens, because images are always resized to one small tile
About 6,404 tokens, because each dimension is tiled twice
About 1,601 tokens, because the image fits into a single tile
About 3,202 tokens, because the width requires two tiles
questions.explanation: Images are tiled in 560 pixel blocks per side, and a 560 by 560 picture gives one tile per side, so the count is one block of 1,601 tokens. Doubling would require a side of about 1,120 pixels, which this image does not reach.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is estimating how much text it can send before hitting a quota or a context limit. Which statements about estimating tokens from characters are correct? Choose three.
options: A planning rule of thumb is about 6 characters per token
For English input to Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, about 4.7 characters equal one token
An exact count requires the model's own tokenizer or the CountTokens operation
One word always equals exactly one token in every model
AWS publishes a single character-to-token ratio that all models share
questions.explanation: AWS publishes 6 characters per token for quota planning and 4.7 characters per token for English input to Titan Text Embeddings V2, and only the tokenizer gives an exact count. Tokenization is model-specific, so words often split across tokens and no single shared ratio exists.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A designer is producing product variants with an image generation model and wants repeatable, controllable results. Which settings steer the generation? Choose four.
options: seed, so the same starting noise reproduces a variant
cfgScale, so adherence to the prompt is tightened or loosened
reference images, with up to 5 supplied in a single request
numberOfImages, so several variants are produced in one call
quality, which selects the tokenizer that splits the prompt
temperature, which tightens how closely the image follows the prompt
questions.explanation: Image models are steered with seed, cfgScale, a limited set of reference images, and numberOfImages. Quality sets fidelity rather than choosing a tokenizer, and temperature is a text sampling parameter that diffusion models do not use.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Put the steps a decoder model follows to produce one completion in the order they occur.
options: Check for a stop condition such as an end token or the output limit
Assemble the prompt from system instructions, context, and conversation history
Fine-tune the model on this prompt before any tokens are produced
Score the vocabulary and sample the next token from the distribution
Count tokens to confirm the prompt fits inside the context window
Append the sampled token and run again with the longer sequence
questions.explanation: Generation is a loop: assemble the prompt, confirm it fits, sample a token, append it, and repeat until a stop condition or the output limit is reached. Fine-tuning is a separate training activity, not a step inside a single completion.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Put the stages of text-to-image generation in the order they occur.
options: Decode the final denoised representation into the output image
Retrieve the closest matching photograph from a stock image library
Encode the text prompt into conditioning for the denoiser
Apply reverse diffusion repeatedly to remove noise under that conditioning
Initialize the latent representation with random noise
questions.explanation: Diffusion conditions on the encoded prompt, starts from random noise, removes it step by step, and then decodes the result into pixels. Nothing is searched or retrieved; the image is generated rather than looked up.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Match each generation parameter to the control it provides.
options: Sets the ceiling on how much the model may generate
Tightens or loosens how randomly tokens are chosen
Nucleus sampling that keeps a cumulative probability mass
Ends generation when a given fragment of text appears
Restricts selection to the k most probable tokens
questions.explanation: Temperature controls randomness, top-p keeps the smallest set above a probability mass, top-k limits candidates, maxTokenCount caps output length, and stopSequences halts generation on a fragment. Confusing top-p with top-k swaps a probability-based filter for a count-based one.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Match each model offered on Amazon Bedrock to what it produces for the caller.
options: Generates or edits images from text and reference images
Accepts text and image input and returns textual analysis
Produces video output from a text prompt
Produces 1024-dimensional vectors representing text
questions.explanation: Nova Reel generates video, Titan Image Generator produces images, Titan Text Embeddings V2 returns a 1,024-dimensional vector, and Llama 3.2 vision models read images and answer in text. An embedding model returns vectors rather than answers, which is the most common mix-up in this set.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A chatbot answers from an internal knowledge base but occasionally invents policy details that are not in any source document. Which action most directly reduces this failure?
options: Raise the temperature so the model produces more varied wording
Increase the maximum output token count so the answer is longer
Add contextual grounding checks that compare the response with the retrieved source
Remove the knowledge base and rely on the model's built-in knowledge
questions.explanation: Contextual grounding checks test whether the generated answer is supported by the retrieved context, which is AWS's documented defense against hallucination. Temperature and output length change style and verbosity rather than factual support, and dropping retrieval makes fabrication more likely.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A compliance reviewer submits the same prompt twice and receives two different answers, then asks which property of generative AI explains this. What is the answer?
options: Hallucination
Nondeterminism
Underfitting
Concept drift
questions.explanation: AWS states that foundation models are nondeterministic, meaning identical inputs can produce different responses. Hallucination means a confident fabrication rather than run-to-run variation, while underfitting and concept drift are classical machine learning terms.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A team must choose a foundation model for a regulated, latency-sensitive customer-facing application. Which set of factors best represents the selection criteria the exam expects?
options: Training data cutoff date, vendor popularity and number of published benchmarks
Only the lowest per-token price and the largest context window
Only the open-source license status of the model weights
Task fit, measured performance, cost, latency, compliance constraints and operational complexity
questions.explanation: AWS frames foundation model selection around the type of model, its performance and capabilities, and the constraints of cost, latency, compliance and complexity. Options that reduce the decision to a single dimension ignore the trade-offs this objective is testing.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A leadership team is reviewing where generative AI helps their business. Which of these are advantages of generative AI that AWS lists?
options: Adaptability, where one model handles many tasks through prompting and fine-tuning
Responsiveness, where output is conditioned on the full context of the prompt
Conversational ability, where a system holds multi-turn dialogue over enterprise data
Interpretability, where every internal step of the model can be read by an auditor
Content generation, where new text, code, images and audio are produced from an instruction
Determinism, where the same prompt always returns a byte-identical response
questions.explanation: AWS lists adaptability, responsiveness, conversational ability and content generation as the four advantages of generative AI. Poor interpretability and nondeterminism appear as disadvantages, so the last two options invert the exam guide's own risk list.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A product team needs to prove that its generative AI feature delivers value to the business. Which metrics belong in that business case?
options: Return on investment from the feature
Conversion rate of users who act on the generated output
F1 score of the underlying classification step
Average revenue per user
Customer lifetime value
Training loss recorded during pre-training
questions.explanation: ROI, conversion rate, average revenue per user and customer lifetime value are business outcome metrics that tie the feature to revenue and efficiency. F1 and training loss are model metrics that describe the algorithm rather than the value delivered.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: An auditor reviewing AI-assisted loan summaries asks which input fields most influenced a particular sentence the assistant produced. The team cannot produce a feature-importance breakdown for generated text. Which disadvantage of generative AI does this illustrate?
options: Nondeterminism, because repeated runs return different sentences for the same input
Poor interpretability, because generated text comes with no readable internal decision rules
Hallucination, because the assistant may invent a reason that appears in no source record
Inaccuracy, because the assistant misreads numeric fields in the source records
questions.explanation: AWS lists poor interpretability as a disadvantage because a foundation model exposes no feature importances or step-by-step rules behind a generated sentence. The other options describe run-to-run variation, unsupported fabrication and wrong facts, which are separate disadvantages.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Before every release, a support team scores its summarizer against a held-out set of reference summaries using ROUGE, BLEU and BERTScore. Which disadvantage of generative AI is this gate designed to catch?
options: Poor interpretability of the model's internal computation
Nondeterminism between two identical inference requests
Lack of conversational ability across multiple turns
Inaccuracy, where generated text drifts away from the correct reference content
questions.explanation: AWS pairs the inaccuracy disadvantage with evaluation on held-out prompt sets and text-overlap metrics such as ROUGE, BLEU and BERTScore, which measure how far output sits from correct references. Interpretability, run-to-run variation and multi-turn dialogue are different properties.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A European insurer must keep customer document processing inside approved EU geographies and passes over a cheaper model hosted elsewhere. Which model-selection factor decides this choice?
options: Compliance and regulatory constraints
Measured performance on the team's benchmark prompts
Operational complexity of running the model
Length of the model's published training data
questions.explanation: AWS lists compliance among the factors for selecting a foundation model, and a hard residency requirement overrides a price difference. Benchmark performance, operational complexity and training-data recency are real considerations but none of them forces this outcome.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A two-person startup with no machine learning staff must ship an assistant in weeks and accepts a slightly weaker model rather than operating training infrastructure. Which selection factor is driving the decision?
options: Cost per token, because the budget is fixed
Latency, because replies must stream quickly
Complexity, meaning how much operational effort the model requires
Compliance, because the customer data is regulated
questions.explanation: AWS includes complexity as a selection factor, and a team without ML staff is trading benchmark quality for lower operational effort. Cost, latency and compliance are valid factors but they are not what the team is buying relief from here.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A media company plans about two million background summarization jobs per month, can wait up to a day for each result, and works to a fixed budget. Which factor should dominate its model choice?
options: Responsiveness of the model in a live conversation
Cost per token of the model
Conversational memory across many turns
Interpretability of the model's internal computation
questions.explanation: AWS lists cost as a selection factor, and very high volume with a fixed budget makes price per token the binding constraint. Responsiveness, multi-turn memory and interpretability describe product qualities rather than the budget pressure in this scenario.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: An in-app assistant must show its first words quickly enough that a chat feels live, and the team will accept a smaller model that answers slightly less well. Which factor is it optimizing?
options: Accuracy measured against a labeled test set
The breadth of providers available in the catalog
The context window size of the model
Latency, meaning the time the user waits for a response
questions.explanation: AWS names latency as a model-selection factor, and trading quality for a faster reply is a latency decision. Accuracy, catalog breadth and context window size matter, but none of them is what the team is optimizing when the response must feel immediate.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Two candidate models have the same price per token, the same latency profile and the same compliance posture. The team runs both on a held-out set of domain prompts and keeps the stronger one. Which factor finally decides the choice?
options: Measured performance on the team's own evaluation set
The number of AWS Regions in which each model is available
The visual design of the provider's console
The month each model was released
questions.explanation: AWS lists performance among the selection factors, and with cost, latency and compliance equal, measured quality on a held-out domain set is the deciding evidence. Region count, console design and release date do not measure model quality.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A billing team must return the same fee result for every customer who enters the same plan and usage values, and the calculation must be auditable line by line. Which approach fits this requirement?
options: A foundation model with a system prompt that demands exact arithmetic
A fine-tuned foundation model, so the fee tables live in the model weights
A rules-based calculation that applies the published fee tables deterministically
A higher temperature setting, so the model explores more candidate answers
questions.explanation: AWS says rules are cheap, low-risk and easy to audit for simple repeatable decisions, while foundation models are nondeterministic. Prompting, fine-tuning and temperature changes cannot turn a generative model into a reliable calculator.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A company has 50,000 labeled emails and needs a spam probability for each incoming message at a very low cost per prediction. Which approach fits best?
options: A generative model asked to explain whether each email is spam
A traditional supervised classification model trained on the labeled emails
A diffusion model that generates example spam messages for review
A rules engine that reads every email word by word
questions.explanation: AWS frames traditional machine learning as the cheaper, faster answer when one narrow labeled task must be done very well, and spam scoring is exactly that task. A generative model adds cost and nondeterminism, a diffusion model produces images, and a word-by-word rule engine will not scale.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A bank builds an assistant for retail support, then reuses it for internal HR answers and measures how well quality holds in the second business area. Which business-value consideration does this measurement describe?
options: Conversion rate of users who act on the generated output
Average revenue per user of the premium tier
Customer lifetime value of the retail segment
Cross-domain performance of the assistant
questions.explanation: Cross-domain performance asks whether a generative AI solution keeps delivering value outside the domain it was first tuned for, which is what the team is measuring. Conversion rate, average revenue per user and customer lifetime value are revenue measures rather than tests of reuse across business areas.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A risk team reviews the failure log of a customer-facing assistant. Which entries are disadvantages of generative AI that AWS names?
options: The assistant states a policy rule that appears in no source document
Two runs of the same summarization prompt return different key figures
Reviewers cannot trace which inputs drove a particular sentence
The assistant needs a labeled dataset before it can answer its first question
A summary misstates a figure that the source document actually contains
The assistant cannot be connected to a source of internal documents
questions.explanation: AWS names four disadvantages: hallucination, nondeterminism, poor interpretability and inaccuracy, and the first, second, third and fifth entries are their operational forms. The two remaining entries are false statements, because assistants work from prompts without labeled data and can be connected to internal sources.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A team is hardening an assistant that sometimes cites support for claims that no source document contains. Which measures does AWS document for reducing that failure?
options: Refine the prompt so the model is told to answer only from provided material
Retrieve relevant passages from an approved knowledge base before generating
Enable contextual grounding checks that score the response against the source
Raise the temperature so wording varies more between runs
Increase the maximum output token count so answers are longer
Remove the system prompt so the model answers with its own knowledge
questions.explanation: AWS's mitigation path runs from prompt refinement to retrieval grounding and contextual grounding checks, which test whether an answer is supported by its source. Raising temperature increases variation, longer outputs do not add evidence, and removing the system prompt makes unsupported answers more likely.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Three months after rollout, a service director wants evidence of operational gains rather than revenue growth. Which measures belong in that review?
options: Average handling time per support case
Share of drafts that agents accept without factual correction
Average revenue per user of the premium subscription
Conversion rate of the sales landing page
Customer lifetime value of the account segment
Training loss recorded when the base model was pre-trained
questions.explanation: Efficiency and accuracy are operational business-value factors, so handling time and the share of drafts that need no correction belong in the review. Revenue per user, conversion rate and lifetime value answer a growth question, and training loss is a model-development measure.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A platform team is writing an incident runbook for variability in model outputs. Which of its notes about nondeterminism are accurate?
options: Identical inputs can produce different responses across runs
Lowering temperature makes outputs more repeatable but does not make them factually reliable
Human review is used where consistent, verified output must be checked
Nondeterminism means the model hides its reasoning from auditors
A larger context window removes nondeterminism completely
Nondeterminism disappears as soon as a model is fine-tuned on company data
questions.explanation: AWS defines foundation models as nondeterministic, treats temperature as the control for sampling variation, and pairs the risk with human review. Poor interpretability, context window size and fine-tuning are unrelated to sampling variation.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each advantage of generative AI that AWS names to a scenario that shows it in action.
options: A legal assistant rewrites clauses, drafts emails and summarizes depositions when the team changes only the prompt
A support bot holds a ten-turn conversation and carries forward what the caller said earlier in the same session
A proposal tool produces a new draft, a product image and a code snippet from a single written instruction
An assistant rebuilds its answer whenever the user edits the constraints in the input, because the whole input conditions the output
questions.explanation: Adaptability is one model serving many tasks through prompting, responsiveness means output is conditioned on the full input, conversational ability is multi-turn dialogue over a session, and content generation produces new text, images or code.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each model-selection factor to the scenario that puts it in the lead.
options: The assistant must call a ticketing API during a conversation, so tool-calling support decides the shortlist
The application generates product images from text, so only models in the image-generation family qualify
Every request must fit in one context window, so models that cannot hold the document in a single pass are excluded
questions.explanation: Type covers which modality family a model belongs to, capabilities cover features such as tool use, and constraints cover hard limits such as context size. AWS names type, capabilities and constraints among the factors for selecting a foundation model.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A team must let users ask questions across 500-page contracts, but the best candidate models accept far less text than that in a single request. Which model-selection factor is driving this design?
options: Compliance requirements
Input and output length constraints
Average revenue per user
Training data volume
questions.explanation: Input and output length is a named selection criterion; when a model's context window cannot hold the document, the design must chunk or map-reduce around that limit.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: The product requires an original illustration for every article, but the shortlisted models generate text only. Which model-selection factor rules them out?
options: Latency
Cost per token
Model complexity
Capabilities
questions.explanation: Capabilities, meaning what modalities and tasks a model supports, is a named selection factor; a text-only model cannot meet an image requirement regardless of its price or speed.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: The exam guide lists specific factors to consider when selecting a GenAI model. Which of these are on that list?
options: Cost
Latency
Model complexity
Performance requirements
The frontend framework the application uses
The number of AWS Regions the company operates in
questions.explanation: The guide's selection factors include model types, performance requirements, capabilities, constraints, compliance, cost, latency and model complexity; implementation details like the frontend or Region count are not model-selection factors.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each outcome to the business-value metric that best measures it.
prompts: Shoppers who consult the assistant complete a purchase more often
The drafting assistant halves the time to produce a policy document
Assistant users spend more per month than non-users
The feature's measurable gains repay its build and run cost
options: Return on investment
Average revenue per user
Conversion rate
Efficiency
questions.explanation: The guide's business-value metrics include conversion rate, efficiency, average revenue per user and ROI, and each scenario maps to exactly one of them.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A marketing team wants fresh campaign-slogan variations from one prompt, while an auditing team must reproduce identical risk scores for identical inputs. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both teams should raise the temperature so every response differs from the last
The scoring team should retry requests until two answers match
Variability helps the slogan task, while the scoring task needs a deterministic approach
Both tasks are fixed by fine-tuning, which guarantees identical outputs
questions.explanation: Foundation models are non-deterministic, and identical inputs can produce different responses, which is an asset for drafting and a liability for scoring an auditor must reproduce, so the scoring path needs deterministic controls or rules instead.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A platform team is writing guidance for choosing foundation models across the company. Which statements belong in that guidance?
options: The best choice depends on the workload, so different tasks may warrant different models
Reassess the choice when requirements change or stronger models become available
Optimizing only for the lowest token price can backfire if rework on errors costs more
The most expensive model produces the best business results for every task
A model's quality in one business area carries over to an unrelated area without testing
Model selection is settled once during the proof of concept and never revisited
questions.explanation: Model choice is workload-specific and should be revisited as needs and options change, and price-only optimization ignores the cost of errors; no model wins on price alone, quality must be re-measured in each domain, and selection is an ongoing decision.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each control to the generative AI advantage it preserves.
options: Content generation
Adaptability
Responsiveness
Conversational ability
questions.explanation: Each advantage depends on a control: budgeting the context window keeps responses responsive to the whole prompt, RAG with Guardrails keeps multi-turn answers grounded, evaluation with human review keeps generated content usable, and the customization spectrum delivers one model across many tasks.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A legal team wants an assistant that reads a 200-page contract and produces one summary of the whole document, and the team plans to use retrieval-augmented generation. How well should it perform?
options: Very well, because retrieval returns the complete document for every question
It is weakest here, because retrieval returns chunks rather than the whole file
It will refuse, because retrieval systems only answer questions and never summarize
It will match fine-tuning, since both approaches see identical source text
questions.explanation: Retrieval supplies relevant chunks, so a whole-document summary can silently omit sections that were never retrieved, which is the documented weakness of retrieval for this shape of task. A refusal would be a design choice rather than a limit of retrieval, and fine-tuning has its own data requirements.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A rules engine already routes refund decisions with deterministic, sub-millisecond responses. A colleague proposes replacing it with a foundation model. What is the strongest reason to keep the rules?
options: It learns from refund history, so its decisions improve without engineering work
It handles edge cases the rules never anticipated by generalizing from patterns
It writes a natural-language rationale for each decision at no extra charge
It adds model cost and latency to work that deterministic logic already does
questions.explanation: Rules give fixed, auditable decisions with no per-request model invocation, so a foundation model would only add cost and latency to a solved problem. Learning from history and generalizing to unseen cases are model behaviors that a rules engine does not have.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A fraud analyst asks what a traditional supervised model produces when it is given a single transaction record. Which answer is correct?
options: A predicted label or numeric score learned from labeled examples
A short narrative describing the transaction in the analyst's own words
A clarifying dialogue turn that asks the analyst what they meant
The original training rows, so the analyst can inspect the source data
questions.explanation: Supervised models map an input to a class or a numeric score, which is exactly what a fraud triage step needs. Producing prose or holding a conversation is generative behavior, and returning training rows is a data-warehouse task.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A shipping rules engine fails on a customer claim the team has never seen before. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The rules ran in a different order, so the same claim produced two results
The engine needs more labeled claims so its classifier can be retrained
No written rule anticipated the case, and rules only cover what was encoded
The engine exceeded its context window and truncated the claim text
questions.explanation: Rules engines execute only the logic engineers wrote, so an unhandled edge case falls through no matter how much data exists. Retraining and context windows describe model-based systems, and rule evaluation itself does not vary between runs.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A team has a repetitive document task where the inputs are messy and inconsistent, there is no labeled dataset, and the output must be flexible prose. Where should it start?
options: Train a supervised classifier, because accuracy is highest once labels exist
Prompt a foundation model and iterate on examples to refine the behavior
Encode the process as rules, since rules absorb messy input without data
Fine-tune a model first, because customization always precedes a prototype
questions.explanation: With messy variable input, no labels, and a need for flexible output, prompt engineering gets a working prototype the team can iterate on quickly. Supervised training needs labels, rules cannot absorb unbounded variation, and fine-tuning comes after a baseline exists.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: An AWS overview states that contextual grounding checks filtered more than 75 percent of hallucinated responses in a tested system. How should a program manager read that figure for a production rollout?
options: Roughly a quarter can still get through, so review and guardrails stay necessary
Hallucinations are solved, so monitoring can stop once the system ships
The rate is guaranteed for every use case without any further testing
Only the model provider can measure hallucinations, so the team should stop
questions.explanation: Filtering more than 75 percent still leaves a minority of unsupported answers reaching users, which is why grounding, guardrails, and human review remain in the design. The figure is an AWS claim about a tested configuration, not a guarantee for every use case.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A team is comparing approaches and wants to know what must already exist before each one can be built. Which statements are correct? Choose four.
options: A rules engine needs no training dataset, only written logic
A traditional supervised model needs labeled examples of the target
Prompting a foundation model needs no labeled dataset to get started
Fine-tuning needs labeled or preference data in the required format
A rules engine must be retrained whenever a regulation changes
A traditional supervised model is steered by rewriting the prompt
questions.explanation: Rules and prompting start from written logic or instructions, while supervised training and fine-tuning both depend on prepared data. Rules are edited rather than retrained, and a supervised model changes only when its training data changes.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: A support team debates retrieval-augmented generation versus fine-tuning for its assistant. Which statements are correct? Choose three.
options: Retrieval leaves the model weights unchanged, while fine-tuning updates them
Fine-tuning requires labeled examples prepared in a training format
Using retrieval together with fine-tuning can beat either approach alone
Retrieval makes the model do correct arithmetic even when the numbers are retrieved
Fine-tuning is the fastest way to reflect a policy change made this morning
questions.explanation: Retrieval injects context at request time without touching weights, whereas fine-tuning changes weights using labeled data and can be combined with retrieval. Retrieval cannot fix the model arithmetic, and a policy change lands faster by updating sources than by retraining.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Put the team selection process in order as it chooses between rules, a predictive model, and generative AI for a new workflow.
options: Pilot the chosen approach and measure results against the defined metric
Buy a foundation model first, then look for a problem it can solve
Define the business outcome and the metric that counts as success
Check whether written rules can already handle the needed cases
Confirm the task genuinely needs generated or unstructured output
Check whether labeled data exists for a narrow supervised predictor
questions.explanation: Selection starts from the outcome and its metric, then tests rules, then labeled prediction, then whether generation is really required, and ends with a measured pilot. Starting from a purchased model inverts the process and risks solving no defined problem.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Rank these approaches from most deterministic to least deterministic in the output they produce, ignoring anything that does not belong in the ranking.
options: A foundation model sampling with a higher temperature
The size of the training dataset, which sets how deterministic output is
A rules engine applying written condition and action pairs
A traditional supervised model returning a predicted class
A foundation model sampling with temperature set to zero
questions.explanation: Rules return exactly one output for a given input, a classifier selects a class, temperature zero makes generation near-reproducible, and higher temperature adds randomness. Dataset size affects accuracy rather than where an approach belongs in this ranking.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each approach to the controls that keep it reliable.
options: Grounding, Guardrails, and human review of the outputs
Unit tests and version-controlled changes to the rules
Offline evaluation, decision thresholds, and monitoring
questions.explanation: Each control set matches the failure mode of its approach: rules break through logic errors, predictors drift or misclassify, and generative output can be unfaithful. Unit tests catch rule defects but not model drift, while monitoring catches drift but says nothing about prompt grounding.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 - Understand the capabilities and limitations of GenAI for solving business problems
questions.question: Match each business need to the type of solution that fits it.
prompts: Routing callers through an interactive voice menu
Estimating how likely a customer is to churn next month
Translating a help article into another language
options: A foundation model generating new content from a prompt
A deterministic script of condition and action pairs
A trained predictor that returns a label or a score
questions.explanation: Menu routing is written logic, churn likelihood is a supervised prediction, and translation is generated content. A predictor returns a number rather than new text, and a rules script cannot produce a fluent translation.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A development team wants to experiment with foundation models from several providers through one serverless API, without provisioning or managing model endpoints. Which service fits?
options: Amazon Bedrock
Amazon Textract
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Lex
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed, serverless service that exposes a single API for foundation models from many providers, so switching models is a change of model ID. Textract, Rekognition and Lex are prebuilt services that answer one narrow task rather than serving general-purpose models.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A customer has steady, predictable production traffic on a custom fine-tuned model and needs capacity reserved ahead of demand. Which Amazon Bedrock capacity option should it use?
options: On-demand inference, which bills only for the tokens actually used
Batch inference, which completes offline jobs within a day
Provisioned throughput, which reserves model capacity for a term
Cross-region inference routing, which spreads traffic across Regions
questions.explanation: Custom fine-tuned models require provisioned throughput, which commits to reserved capacity billed by time rather than purely by tokens. On-demand suits spiky usage, batch suits offline bulk work, and cross-region routing is about cost and latency placement rather than reservation.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: An enterprise is building a business case for using AWS generative AI services. Which benefits does AWS associate with these services?
options: Access to a broad selection of foundation models through a single managed API
Lower operational overhead because AWS manages the underlying infrastructure and scaling
Security and compliance capabilities that work with the shared responsibility model
Complete transfer of data governance and access control responsibility to AWS
Faster time to market by starting from pre-trained models instead of building from scratch
A guarantee of the lowest inference cost across every cloud provider
questions.explanation: AWS frames its generative AI services around accessibility, a lower barrier to entry, efficiency, cost-effectiveness and speed to market, alongside security and compliance under shared responsibility. Customers retain responsibility for their own data and access control, and no provider can promise the lowest cost for every workload.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: Place these steps of a generative AI project on AWS in the order a team typically performs them.
options: Monitor the released application for cost, quality and safety
Select a foundation model and iterate on prompts with sample inputs
Evaluate the application against a held-out set of test prompts
Define the business use case and the success criteria
Ground the application with a knowledge base over internal documents
questions.explanation: The project starts from a defined business use case, then moves to model selection and prompting, grounding on internal data, evaluation against held-out prompts, and finally production monitoring. Evaluation must come after the application is built and before release, and monitoring only exists once the application is running.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: Match each AWS generative AI service to the capability it provides.
options: A managed runtime with tool gateway, memory and observability components for production agents
A serverless API for invoking and customizing foundation models from many providers
An open-source SDK for building and testing AI agents
A model hub for discovering, fine-tuning and deploying pre-trained models with minimal code
An environment for building, training and deploying custom machine learning models with full control
questions.explanation: Bedrock serves foundation models through one serverless API, SageMaker AI builds and trains custom machine learning models, JumpStart accelerates use of pre-trained models, Strands Agents is an open-source agent SDK, and AgentCore provides the managed runtime, tools and memory for production agents.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A team routes assistant traffic through a global inference profile because it is roughly 10 percent cheaper, accepting that requests may run in AWS Regions it has not enabled. Which cost tradeoff did it make?
options: Regional coverage, where broader routing lowers cost but reduces control over where processing happens
Responsiveness, where cheaper routing queues requests behind other customers' traffic
Redundancy, where the application now runs without a standby copy in another Region
Performance, where the profile silently serves a smaller model to stay within budget
questions.explanation: AWS documents the global profile as about 10% cheaper with processing allowed in any commercial Region, while a geographic profile keeps work inside a US, EU or APAC geography. The saving buys Region placement flexibility, not queueing, standby capacity or a model downgrade.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A data team finds that its first-choice model costs several times more per token but produces materially fewer factual errors in long document analysis, and the budget has room. Which cost tradeoff is the team accepting?
options: Availability, because a pricier model needs a standby copy
Redundancy, because capacity must be replicated across Availability Zones
Performance, paying more per token for better output quality
Responsiveness, because longer answers queue behind other traffic
questions.explanation: AWS frames cost and performance as a tradeoff in model selection, and spending more per token to reduce factual errors buys quality with budget. Availability, redundancy and responsiveness are different tradeoffs and are not what the extra spend is purchasing here.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: To reduce spend, a company runs its assistant backend in one AWS Region with no standby deployment. Which tradeoff has it accepted?
options: Lower model quality, because a single Region serves a smaller traffic pool
Higher token prices, because single-Region workloads lose volume discounts
Slower responses, because requests must travel to a distant Region
Reduced redundancy and availability, because a Regional outage takes the application down
questions.explanation: AWS presents redundancy and availability as benefits that multi-Region or standby designs buy, and dropping that design saves money at the cost of Regional failure coverage. Model quality, token pricing and request distance do not follow from choosing one Region.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A company holds its own open-weights model and wants to serve it through a managed API without a training job or an hourly capacity commitment. Which option fits?
options: Supervised fine-tuning of a Bedrock base model served on provisioned capacity
Custom Model Import, which serves your own weights and can run on on-demand pricing
Batch inference, which loads the weights fresh for each offline job
A global inference profile, which mirrors your weights into other Regions
questions.explanation: Custom Model Import is AWS's documented path for bringing your own weights into Bedrock, and it can run on-demand unlike a supervised fine-tuned model that requires Provisioned Throughput. Batch is a pricing mode for hosted models, and profiles only route traffic.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 - Describe AWS infrastructure and technologies for building GenAI applications
questions.question: A customer's security team asks whether prompts sent to a third-party model on Amazon Bedrock can reach that model's vendor or be used to train the shared base model. Which answer matches AWS documentation?
options: Inputs and outputs are not shared with third-party model providers and are not used to train the base models
