questions.explanation: Controllability is defined as having mechanisms to monitor and steer AI system behavior, which is exactly what a pause-and-override capability provides; veracity, inclusivity and provider governance cover different concerns.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A question-answering assistant over an internal policy PDF occasionally invents coverage limits that appear nowhere in the source document. A guardrail is attached and its content filters pass every response. Which change most directly addresses the problem?
options: Raise the content filter strength to HIGH so inaccurate text is blocked
Add a denied topic so the assistant refuses questions about coverage
Enable trace mode so every evaluation score is returned to the caller
Enable a contextual grounding check that scores the response against the source
questions.explanation: Contextual grounding checks score faithfulness to the supplied source and relevance to the query, with thresholds from 0 to 0.99 on the output side; content filter strength covers harm categories, denied topics block subjects, and trace mode only reports findings.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A fraud-detection model reports 98% accuracy yet flags almost no fraudulent transactions; only 2% of its training rows are labeled fraudulent. Which dataset characteristic best explains the misleading accuracy?
options: Class imbalance, which lets a majority-class predictor look accurate
Insufficient curation, which left duplicate records in the training set
Excessive diversity, which raised the model's variance
Missing features, which caused the model to underfit
questions.explanation: With a 2% positive class, a model can score 98% by predicting the majority class every time, so a balanced dataset or metrics such as precision and recall are needed to expose the failure.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A credit-risk model scores 96% on its training data but 74% on the held-out evaluation set, and its remaining errors cluster among applicants with little credit history, whose rows made up only a few dozen training examples each. Which diagnosis best fits these symptoms?
options: Underfitting, because the model is too simple for every segment
Overfitting, because memorized patterns fail to generalize in sparsely represented segments
Data leakage, because the label is present in the input features
Class imbalance, because the evaluation set over-represents large segments
questions.explanation: A large train-to-evaluation gap with errors concentrated where data is scarce is the signature of high variance (overfitting); underfitting would score poorly on both sets rather than only on unseen data.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Reviewers discover that annotators applied the 'escalate' guideline differently to casual text messages than to formal ones, and the model now reproduces that difference in production. Which analysis should the team run first?
options: A subgroup analysis of error rates over six months of production traffic
A review of the guardrail's content filter strengths
A global SHAP aggregation over the full training dataset
A label-quality analysis comparing annotations with the written guideline
questions.explanation: When the labels themselves are applied inconsistently the model faithfully learns the inconsistency, so auditing label quality against the guideline comes first; subgroup analysis and SHAP diagnose the model rather than the annotations.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A bank's assistant must never output the exact name of a rival bank. Which guardrail safeguard fits best, given how each one matches content?
options: A denied topic, because topics are matched contextually in natural language
Content filters at strength MEDIUM, because they classify against harm categories
A word filter, because it matches case-insensitive whole words and phrases exactly
A sensitive information filter, because a bank name is an entity type it detects
questions.explanation: AWS documents word filters as case-insensitive whole-word and whole-phrase exact matching, which suits a specific name; denied topics are meant for subjects, and AWS warns against using them to capture individual entity names.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A moderation assistant reliably refuses harmful requests, but inserting extra spaces or unusual punctuation into the same request makes it comply. Which responsible AI dimension is failing?
options: Veracity, meaning factual correctness of the response
Fairness, meaning equal treatment across stakeholder groups
Robustness, meaning correct output for expected and unexpected inputs
Inclusivity, meaning coverage of languages and populations
questions.explanation: Robustness is defined as achieving correct system outputs for both expected and unexpected inputs, and small input perturbations are the classic unexpected-input case; the other dimensions describe unrelated properties.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Two foundation models meet the accuracy bar for an internal summarization task. One runs on a dedicated endpoint provisioned around the clock; the other is invoked on demand and scales to zero when idle. Which consideration favors the second choice?
options: Environmental sustainability, because provisioned but idle capacity still consumes resources
Veracity, because on-demand models return more factually correct outputs
Inclusivity, because serverless endpoints accept a wider range of input languages
Controllability, because scaling to zero removes the need for human oversight
questions.explanation: AWS's responsible selection guidance is to choose right-sized components and avoid over-provisioned or inefficient resources so energy use stays proportional to real need; the other options misuse unrelated responsible AI dimensions.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team needs bias measurements across demographic facets for a deployed tabular credit model, plus feature attributions behind individual decisions. Which AWS capability is designed for that job?
options: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, which filters prompts and responses
Amazon SageMaker Clarify, which computes bias metrics and SHAP attributions
Amazon Rekognition, which moderates image and video content
Amazon CloudWatch, which stores metrics and logs
questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides pre-training and post-training bias metrics together with SHAP local and global attributions for tabular models; Guardrails filter content rather than measuring bias, and Rekognition and CloudWatch serve unrelated purposes.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team is mapping its ML system against the AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens dimensions. Which statements pair a dimension with what it actually covers?
options: Controllability - mechanisms that let operators monitor and steer system behavior
Veracity - achieving factually correct system outputs
Fairness - considering impacts on different groups of stakeholders
Safety - guaranteeing that every model output is accurate
Privacy - measuring how evenly errors are distributed across demographic groups
Robustness - keeping inference latency stable under heavy load
questions.explanation: AWS defines controllability as monitoring and steering behavior, veracity as factually correct outputs, and fairness as impacts across stakeholder groups; safety is about blocking harmful output, privacy is about data handling, and robustness is about correctness under unexpected inputs.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Which of these are legal or business risks that an AI review board should log for a customer-facing GenAI feature?
options: Third parties claim the assistant's outputs reproduce copyrighted material
Stereotyped outputs damage customer trust in the brand
A user acts on an invented answer and suffers a real loss
The assistant states fabricated information as fact
The model provider absorbs your application's legal liability under the shared responsibility model
Enabling guardrails removes every remaining legal risk from the feature
questions.explanation: AWS's list of GenAI legal risks covers intellectual property infringement claims, biased model outputs, loss of customer trust, end user risk and hallucinations; liability stays with the customer under the shared responsibility model and guardrails reduce but never eliminate risk.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Which statements about Amazon Bedrock Guardrails are accurate?
options: A guardrail must be attached explicitly, because Bedrock does not apply one to every call automatically
The same guardrail can be attached to different models, agents and knowledge bases
ApplyGuardrail can evaluate text without invoking any foundation model
Guardrails measure statistical bias in a training dataset before a model is deployed
Content filters and word filters both use semantic similarity to catch misspelled words
Guardrails evaluate reasoning content blocks as well as prompts and responses
questions.explanation: Guardrails are optional by default and must be attached explicitly, are reusable across models, agents and knowledge bases, and ApplyGuardrail runs them standalone; bias measurement belongs to SageMaker Clarify, word filters match exactly, and content filters exclude reasoning content.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Place the steps of a pre-deployment subgroup bias assessment in the order they occur.
options: Audit label quality for those groups against the written guidelines
Compute error and outcome rates separately for each subgroup
Compare subgroup results against the agreed fairness threshold
Document the findings and the remediation plan before release
Raise the model's sampling temperature to widen output diversity
Define the demographic groups and the metrics that will be compared
questions.explanation: Assessment fixes the groups and metrics first, then checks whether the labels are trustworthy, then measures per-group outcomes, then judges them against a threshold, and only then documents the result; changing sampling temperature is unrelated to bias assessment.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Place the steps of a responsible foundation model selection review in the order they occur.
options: Shortlist candidate models that satisfy the stated requirements
Evaluate the shortlisted models against the same test criteria
Of the models that pass evaluation, compare footprint and resource efficiency
Record the selection and its tradeoffs in a model card
Fine-tune the selected model on proprietary customer data
State the accuracy, safety and transparency requirements for the use case
questions.explanation: Requirements come first, then a shortlist, then a common evaluation, then the environmental and efficiency comparison among survivors, and finally documentation; fine-tuning is an implementation step that happens after the selection review ends.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Match each Amazon Bedrock Guardrails safeguard to what it actually does.
options: Scores response faithfulness to a source on a 0 to 0.99 scale
Matches predefined harm categories such as hate and prompt attack
Detects PII entities and blocks or masks them
Blocks subjects you define in natural language, up to 30 per guardrail
Matches exact whole words and phrases, including managed lists
questions.explanation: Each safeguard answers a different question: harm category, subject, exact string, personal data, or faithfulness to a source, and mixing them up is the classic Guardrails error.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Match each bias detection technique to what it examines.
options: Recomputes predictions while changing only a sensitive attribute
Raters read individual cases and judge whether outcomes were fair
Checks whether the annotations themselves follow the written guideline
Measures class imbalance and label distribution before training
Breaks metrics down by demographic segment and compares them
questions.explanation: The techniques differ by what they inspect: the annotations, individual cases, per-group metrics, the raw label distribution, or a single-attribute change, and choosing the wrong one lets a broken pipeline pass review.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A moderation model flags benign messages from one community far more often than from every other community. Its training corpus is almost entirely formal written English, while the flagged messages lean on regional slang and informal phrasing. Which dataset characteristic best explains the disparity?
options: Insufficient curation, which left duplicate messages from the majority community in the corpus
Class imbalance, because benign messages outnumber abusive messages overall
Insufficient inclusivity and diversity, because the corpus under-represents how the affected community writes
Overfitting, because the model memorized the training corpus
questions.explanation: When a corpus under-represents the language patterns of one group the model never learns them and produces higher error rates for that group; an overall benign-versus-abusive imbalance, duplicate records and memorization would not produce a disparity tied to a single community's writing style.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A stakeholder says a forecasting model is biased because its average prediction sits below the true values for every group, and a second stakeholder uses the same word for loan approval rates that differ sharply by demographic group. Which statement resolves the two uses?
options: Both describe the same defect, so one bias measurement can report on them together
They are different senses of the word: systematic error in the predictions on one hand, unequal outcomes between groups on the other, and each is measured differently
The first is a data-collection problem and the second is a model-architecture problem
Only the second use is valid, because the word bias is reserved for annotation errors
questions.explanation: The exam guide itself uses bias in both senses, but they are diagnosed with different measurements, so one number cannot answer both questions. Systematic error in predictions and unequal outcomes between groups are separate defects.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A leadership team asks how to reduce the environmental footprint of a high-volume generative AI feature without changing what users see. Which practices belong in the plan?
options: Route simple high-volume requests to the smallest model that meets the quality bar
Prefer the largest available model for every request to maximize quality
Batch non-urgent generation instead of running it interactively
Keep every endpoint provisioned around the clock to avoid cold starts
Limit output length to what the task actually needs
Process every request synchronously even when the user can tolerate a delay
questions.explanation: Right-sized models, batched non-urgent work and trimmed output lengths all cut compute per request while the user experience stays the same. Bigger models, always-on capacity and synchronous handling of delay-tolerant traffic all raise resource use for no benefit.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Match each bias mitigation action to the stage of the ML lifecycle where it is applied.
prompts: Resample or reweight the training records so small groups are represented
Add a fairness constraint to the objective the training job optimizes
Adjust the decision cutoff applied to each group's scores
Alert when measured bias on live traffic crosses an agreed threshold
options: After training, on the model's scored outputs
After deployment, on live production data
Before training, on the raw training data
During training, inside the objective function
questions.explanation: AWS documents mitigation before training by changing the data, during training by constraining the objective, and after training by adjusting outputs, plus monitoring once the model serves live traffic. Detection measures the problem; it never removes it.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A compliance team needs its assistant to state whether an answer about refunds breaks a written company policy, and to name the rule it breaks rather than return a score. Which capability fits that requirement?
options: An Automated Reasoning check that formalizes the policy document and returns findings such as VALID and INVALID
A contextual grounding check that returns a numeric faithfulness score between 0 and 0.99
A content filter raised to HIGH on the Misconduct category
A denied topic that makes the assistant refuse any question containing the word refund
questions.explanation: Automated Reasoning checks translate a policy document into formal logic and report a finding that cites the violated rule, while a grounding check only returns probabilistic scores against source text and content filters target harmful material rather than policy breaches.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A guardrail's content filter for the Violence category is configured with strength MEDIUM on both input and output. Which behavior results?
options: Only content classified as exactly MEDIUM confidence is blocked, and HIGH confidence passes through
Content classified as HIGH or MEDIUM confidence is blocked, while LOW confidence passes
Content classified as LOW confidence or above is blocked, because MEDIUM includes LOW
Nothing is blocked until the strength is raised to HIGH on the output side
questions.explanation: Strengths are cumulative rather than exact matches: MEDIUM blocks HIGH and MEDIUM classifications and lets LOW pass, LOW blocks only HIGH, and NONE blocks nothing at all.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team wants its guardrail to catch system-prompt extraction attempts written in German, and it plans to stay on the Classic tier. Which statement is accurate?
options: Both tiers detect prompt leakage, but Classic covers English only
Classic already covers English, French and German, so the requirement is met
Prompt-leakage detection is a Standard-tier capability, and Standard also raises supported languages to as many as 60
Prompt leakage is handled by the word filter, so the tier choice makes no difference
questions.explanation: Prompt-leakage detection ships on the Standard tier only, and Standard extends language coverage to as many as 60 languages while Classic covers English, French and Spanish, so German coverage needs the Standard tier.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team sets both inputAction and outputAction to NONE for the US_SOCIAL_SECURITY_NUMBER entity while it calibrates a guardrail in staging. What happens when that entity is detected?
options: The span is replaced with a placeholder before the model ever sees it
The whole message is replaced by the configured blocked-content string
The detection is recorded in the guardrail trace and nothing else changes
An error is returned to the caller so the user can correct the input
questions.explanation: NONE is the detect-only setting: the guardrail observes and records the finding for tuning without masking or blocking, which is why it belongs in staging before go-live rather than as a permanent production state.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team runs the prompt-attack filter over the whole Converse request, including its own system prompt, and legitimate turns now get flagged as attacks. Which change addresses this?
options: Raise the Prompt Attack strength to HIGH so the filter learns to ignore developer instructions
Wrap the system prompt in guardContent tags as well, so both sides of the request are evaluated
Move the system prompt into a denied topic so the filter never inspects it
Tag only the untrusted user content with guardContent and leave the system prompt outside it, using a random tag suffix per request
questions.explanation: The prompt-attack filter must evaluate only the tagged block of user content, because trusted developer instructions such as a refusal rule contain exactly the words the filter looks for, and the tag suffix should be randomized so it cannot be predicted.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Which statement about contextual grounding checks is accurate?
options: They evaluate the prompt and the response, and the threshold may be set to 1.00
They score retrieved chunks before the model runs, so no response text is required
They score only the generated response, against a grounding source and a query, with a threshold from 0 to 0.99
They are designed for open-ended chatbots, where there is no source document
questions.explanation: The check runs on output only, needs both a grounding source and a query, and accepts thresholds from 0 to 0.99 because 1 is invalid, which is why AWS states it is not designed for open-ended chatbots with no source to be faithful to.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A platform team is making guardrails mandatory across its organization. Which statements about guardrail versions and enforcement are correct?
options: An enforced guardrail must be a numbered version, because DRAFT cannot be enforced
The DRAFT version stays editable while a numbered version created from it is immutable
Sharing a guardrail with another account takes a resource policy on the guardrail itself
Attaching a guardrail to one model makes it apply to every application in the account
Blocked-content messaging can be customized so refusals match the organization's wording
An organization-wide rule can be expressed by an Allow on bedrock:InvokeModel in an identity policy
questions.explanation: Enforced guardrails must be numeric, DRAFT is mutable while numbered versions are frozen, cross-account sharing needs a resource policy, and blocked messaging is configurable; attaching a guardrail covers only the resource it is attached to, and an Allow never enforces anything.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: A team is promoting a guardrail configuration from staging to production. Which statements about that move are correct?
options: Sensitive-information detection is probabilistic and context dependent, so thresholds are calibrated with detect-only mode before go-live
Guardrails measure bias across demographic groups, so a separate bias assessment is unnecessary
When model invocation logging is on, blocked content is stored in plain text in the model invocation logs
The guardrail trace returns the original triggering text, so trace should stay disabled in production
Grounding and relevance thresholds are whole numbers from 1 to 5, so they behave like ratings
Turning off evaluation for an entity type means that entity is not billed
questions.explanation: Detection is probabilistic and therefore tuned first, blocked content lands in plain text when logging is on, the trace hands back the triggering text, and disabled entities are not billed; bias measurement belongs to Clarify and Bedrock Model Evaluations, and thresholds run from 0 to 0.99.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Place the steps of rolling out an Amazon Bedrock guardrail in the order the team carries them out.
options: Safeguards such as content filters, denied topics and grounding are configured on the DRAFT
Candidate inputs and outputs are passed to ApplyGuardrail so the team can see which interventions fire
A numbered version is created from the tested DRAFT
The running workload is pinned to that numeric version rather than to DRAFT
The guardrail is deleted and re-created at every release so the configuration starts fresh
The guardrail is created and opens as the automatically created DRAFT version
questions.explanation: The guardrail starts life as DRAFT, gets configured, is exercised with ApplyGuardrail to observe the interventions, is published as an immutable numbered version, and only then is that version pinned by the workload, because re-creating the guardrail would discard the tested configuration.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Place the steps of a pre-launch red-team exercise for a customer-facing assistant in the order the team performs them.
options: Jailbreak, injection and edge-case prompts are written against those failure modes
The intended use, known limitations and risk cases are documented so the team knows what to attack
Escapes and interventions from the run are logged as findings with owners and due dates
The prompts are run against a staging guardrail version rather than against production
Safeguards are tuned and the exercise is repeated to confirm the finding rate falls
The assistant is promoted to production before any adversarial prompt is written
questions.explanation: A red team starts from documented intended use and limitations, writes attacks for those risks, runs them against staging, records the findings, then tunes and re-runs; promoting first would ship the assistant before anyone probed it.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Match each post-training bias metric to the question it answers.
options: How much do true positive rates differ across the facets?
Does flipping the sensitive attribute change the prediction?
What is the ratio of positive prediction rates across facets?
How much does accuracy differ across the facets?
questions.explanation: Disparate Impact is a ratio of positive prediction rates, Accuracy Difference compares accuracy between facets, Recall Difference compares true positive rates, and the Counterfactual Fliptest changes the sensitive attribute to see whether the label flips.

questions.subdomain: 4.1 - Explain the development of AI systems that are responsible
questions.question: Match each content-filter category to the kind of content it targets.
options: Jailbreaks, injection and system-prompt extraction attempts
Descriptions or praise of physical harm and weapons
Prejudice or hostility toward a protected group
Language that condones unlawful acts such as fraud
Demeaning or mocking language aimed at a person
questions.explanation: Hate targets hostility toward protected groups, Insults targets demeaning language, Misconduct targets content that condones unlawful acts, Violence targets harm and weapons, and Prompt Attack targets jailbreaks, injection and prompt extraction.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A regulator asks a bank to show the documented background of the credit model in production, including intended use, training data, evaluation results and approval status. Which artifact should the team produce?
options: The AWS CloudTrail record of the most recent model invocation
The AWS Artifact page listing the bank's own compliance agreements
The Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluations report scored by an LLM-as-a-judge
The SageMaker Model Card registered with the model package
questions.explanation: A SageMaker Model Card is the per-model record of dataset, metrics, evaluation results, intended use and approval status. CloudTrail records API calls, AWS Artifact holds AWS's own compliance reports, and an evaluation report scores outputs without documenting the model's background.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A regulated insurer must give a customer a clear reason whenever an application is declined. One candidate model scores higher on accuracy but produces decisions the team cannot trace, while a simpler model is fully traceable. Which consideration should decide the choice?
options: Whether each decision can be explained to the affected customer, even if that costs some measured accuracy
Whether the higher-scoring model can ship first and be documented later if a regulator asks
Whether the model's weights are open source, since published weights make decisions explainable
Whether the simpler model has lower inference latency, since faster answers appear more credible
questions.explanation: The documented trade-off is interpretability against performance, and a duty to explain individual decisions bounds how much accuracy a team may buy. Shipping first and documenting later, open weights and lower latency do not make a specific decision traceable.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Place the steps of an explainability and documentation review for a model in the order they occur.
options: Publish the approved model card so auditors can retrieve it from the model registry
Define the intended use, intended users and known limitations of the model
Run the model against a representative evaluation dataset
Generate feature attributions and subgroup metrics for the evaluated predictions
Review the results with human subject-matter experts and record the open questions
questions.explanation: A team cannot judge what a model explains until it states what the model is for, and evidence must exist before experts can review it or a card can be published. Intended use, evaluation, attribution, expert review and publication is the only defensible sequence.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each transparency tool to the purpose it serves.
prompts: Published model license and training-data documentation
options: Reveals how a third-party model may be used and where its training data came from
Records the intended use, data, metrics and approval status of a model your team built
Scores candidate models against a dataset using automatic, human or LLM-as-a-judge criteria
Describes AWS's own AI services, including intended uses, limitations and design choices
questions.explanation: Model Cards document your own model, Bedrock Model Evaluations scores candidate outputs, AI Service Cards document AWS's services, and third-party license and data documentation shows permitted use and provenance. Each tool answers a different transparency question.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A lender must explain one declined application to the applicant, and separately show regulators which features drive the model's behavior across the portfolio. Which pairing of explanation types fits both needs?
options: A local explanation for the individual decision and a global explanation for portfolio behavior
A global explanation for the individual decision and a local explanation for portfolio behavior
A model card for the individual decision and a training log for portfolio behavior
A benchmark score for the individual decision and a data sheet for portfolio behavior
questions.explanation: Local explanations attribute one prediction, while global explanations summarize feature influence across many predictions. Both are produced by tools such as SageMaker Clarify SHAP analysis.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Place the steps a lender follows when a customer asks for the reason behind an automated credit decision in the order they occur.
options: Deliver the reason and the appeal path to the customer
Retrieve the decision record, the input features and the model version used
Have a reviewer check the explanation against policy and plain-language guidance
Generate local feature attributions for that specific prediction
Publish a new global benchmark score before responding
questions.explanation: The response starts from the recorded decision and model version, generates a local explanation, has it reviewed, and then communicates it with an appeal path.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each audience to the transparency artifact that best serves it.
options: Plain-language reason and appeal path for the decision
Model card with intended use, metrics and approval status
CloudTrail records of invocation identity and time
SHAP values for that individual prediction
questions.explanation: Each audience needs a different artifact: approval evidence for the regulator, per-prediction attributions for the data scientist, a plain-language reason for the customer, and invocation records for the auditor.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A team is choosing between a logistic regression whose coefficients can be read directly and a gradient-boosted model that will be explained afterward with SHAP. Which statement is correct?
options: The logistic regression is inherently transparent, while the boosted model is only explainable after the fact
Both models are equally transparent once SHAP explanations are generated
The boosted model is transparent because an approved tool produces its explanations
The logistic regression cannot be explained because it has no SHAP values
questions.explanation: A model that exposes its own decision logic is transparent without extra tooling, while a complex model becomes explainable only through post-hoc attributions such as SHAP, which approximate rather than reveal the model's internals.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Two analysts run SHAP on the same trained model and report different top features for the same population. Which statement best explains the difference?
options: SHAP produces only global values, so the two reports must be averaged
The analysts chose different baselines, and SHAP explanations are contrastive to the baseline
SHAP results are random, so identical runs cannot be expected to agree
The model was retrained between runs, which invalidates both reports
questions.explanation: AWS documents that explanations are contrastive and that different baselines yield different explanations for the same prediction, so the baseline must be chosen deliberately and recorded; SHAP produces both local and global values and is reproducible for a fixed configuration.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A team wants to verify an external model provider's accuracy and safety claims independently instead of taking them on faith. Which option gives the team the most transparency?
options: A hosted API model described only by a vendor marketing page
A larger proprietary model that leads the public leaderboards
An openly licensed model whose weights and documentation can be inspected locally
A proprietary model whose details are covered by a non-disclosure agreement
questions.explanation: The exam guide lists open source models, data and licensing as tools for identifying transparent and explainable models, because open weights let you inspect and evaluate the model yourself instead of trusting the provider's claims.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes transparency from explainability?
options: Transparency is disclosing and documenting that and how AI is used, while explainability is why a particular output was produced
Transparency is why one prediction happened, while explainability is whether the system is documented
Transparency and explainability are two names for publishing the model's source code
Transparency applies to image models and explainability applies to text models
questions.explanation: Transparency covers disclosure and documentation of the system itself, while explainability addresses the reasons behind individual outputs, so a system can be fully documented yet still opaque about a single decision.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A low-stakes internal triage tool routes support tickets to the right team, and no stakeholder requires reasons for individual routes. Which reasoning best supports the final model choice?
options: Pick the rules-based model, because transparency always outweighs accuracy
Pick the rules-based model, because internal tools are exempt from responsible AI
Pick the complex model, because higher accuracy automatically means greater trustworthiness
Pick the complex model, because interpretability should be weighed against performance for the use case
questions.explanation: The guide frames the tradeoff as measuring interpretability against performance for the specific use case, so with low risk and no explanation obligation performance can legitimately win, while high-stakes regulated uses reverse that answer.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Which practices reflect human-centered design for explainable AI?
options: Prototype explanations with representative users and revise what they misunderstand
Provide a channel for users to flag confusing or wrong explanations
Test comprehension with the people who will actually receive the explanations
Design explanations for data scientists only and release them unchanged
Publish model weights and training code as the main user-facing explanation
questions.explanation: Human-centered design iterates with real users and keeps a feedback loop open, so explanations are tested with the intended audience and revised from their input; targeting only data scientists or dumping raw artifacts is not user-centered.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Which statements about SageMaker Model Cards are accurate?
options: A new card starts in DRAFT status and moves through review states
Edits create new versions, preserving an immutable record of what was documented
They can be exported to PDF and shared with reviewers and regulators
They update themselves automatically when production drift is detected
They document AWS's own AI services rather than your model
questions.explanation: Model cards are the versioned, immutable documentation artifact for your own model, default to DRAFT, and export to PDF; drift monitoring belongs to SageMaker Model Monitor, and AWS's own services are documented in AI Service Cards.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Which statements correctly describe the tradeoff between model safety and transparency?
options: A simpler interpretable model may give up accuracy relative to a complex one
A complex model may be more accurate but support only approximate post-hoc explanations
The acceptable balance depends on the risk and obligations of the use case
Safety and transparency always improve at the same time, so no tension exists
Selecting the highest-scoring model on a benchmark satisfies transparency requirements
questions.explanation: The guide names the tradeoff as interpretability versus performance, which means the balance is set per use case; the claims that safety and transparency always rise together, or that benchmark scores substitute for transparency, are false.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Place the steps that turn model attributions into a user-facing explanation in the order they occur.
options: Select the inputs that contributed most strongly to that decision
Rewrite the technical feature names into the user's own terms
Present the reasons alongside the outcome the user received
Attach the explanation to the decision record for later audit
Retrain the model immediately on the user's feedback
Compute local attributions for the individual decision
questions.explanation: The pipeline runs from computation to selection to translation to presentation, with the explanation recorded for audit afterward; retraining on feedback is a separate model-maintenance activity, not part of producing an explanation.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Place the steps of a licensing and openness due diligence review in the order they occur.
options: For those models, compare license terms and usage restrictions
Assess what your team can verify independently instead of trusting the provider
Record any remaining reliance on provider-only disclosures in the model card
Fine-tune the selected model on proprietary customer data
Identify which candidate models publish open weights, documentation and evaluations
questions.explanation: Openness facts are gathered first, then license terms are compared, then the team judges what it can verify itself, and the residual reliance is documented; fine-tuning happens only after the review concludes.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each explanation failure to what is wrong with it.
prompts: A raw SHAP summary plot handed to a loan applicant
A confidence score offered as the reason for a decline
Overall accuracy published as the only disclosure
An architecture description sent instead of a decision reason
Reasons withheld to keep the model's logic secret
options: A number that does not identify the inputs behind the outcome
Details the system rather than why this outcome happened
A figure the recipient cannot interpret or act on
Aggregate performance offered where individual reasons are owed
Transparency lost, with no path for the affected person to respond
questions.explanation: Each pair links a specific explanation failure to its consequence: raw charts do not communicate, confidence is not a reason, aggregates are not individual reasons, architecture is not a decision reason, and secrecy removes accountability.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A media company wants anyone who receives an exported image to be able to verify that it came from the company's generative model, even after the file is re-shared. Which approach meets the requirement?
options: Publish the model's intended use in a model card and link to it
Keep generated images in a private S3 bucket with access logs
Embed an invisible watermark and C2PA content credentials at generation time
Lower the sampling temperature so images vary less
questions.explanation: AWS image generators embed an invisible watermark in the pixels and C2PA content credentials as metadata, so verification travels with the file itself. Documentation, storage controls and sampling settings do not travel with an exported image.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Place these transparency mechanisms in order from the one that explains a single decision to the one that documents the broadest scope.
options: A model card describing the team's model, its data and its evaluation
A re-run of the accuracy benchmark on the held-out test set
Feature attributions for one declined application
The provider's AI service card describing intended uses and limitations
Aggregate feature importance computed across the whole portfolio
questions.explanation: Scope widens from one decision, to the model's behavior across all cases, to the team's documented model, and finally to the provider's whole service. Re-running a benchmark measures performance rather than explaining anything.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each transparency artifact to what it cannot establish on its own.
prompts: The model card for the model your team built
The AI service card AWS publishes for an AI service
A SHAP attribution for one prediction
An invisible watermark embedded in a generated image
options: Whether your team configured and used the service appropriately
Whether the image's content is factually true
Why one specific applicant was declined
Whether outcomes are fair across demographic groups
questions.explanation: Each artifact answers one kind of question: documentation of your own model, the provider's own service limits, the features behind one prediction, and the provenance of an image. None of them covers the others' ground, which is where transparency reviews usually fail.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A stakeholder asks what a partial dependence plot shows for a tabular model. Which answer is correct?
options: The marginal effect of one feature on the prediction as that feature varies
The share of the model's total error attributable to each feature
The accuracy gap between two candidate models on the same test set
The probability that a positive prediction is in fact wrong
questions.explanation: Partial dependence isolates how the prediction moves as one feature changes while the others are held at observed values, whereas feature contributions to one prediction come from SHAP and the other options describe evaluation metrics rather than explanations.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A newsroom wants to confirm that an uploaded picture came from its own generative pipeline. Which statement about Amazon Bedrock watermark detection is accurate?
options: It recognizes any AI-generated image regardless of which model produced it
In the console it detects watermarks from Amazon Titan Image Generator and Amazon Nova Canvas in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon)
It works in every Region but only for images already stored in the account's S3 bucket
It replaces C2PA content credentials, so provenance metadata no longer travels with the file
questions.explanation: Console watermark detection covers the watermarks of Amazon Titan Image Generator and Amazon Nova Canvas in the two US Regions, it does not recognize arbitrary third-party output, and it complements rather than replaces C2PA content credentials.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A marketing lead wants to advertise that the company's assistant is NIST certified because the team followed the NIST AI RMF. Which correction is accurate?
options: The AI RMF is a voluntary framework with no certification scheme, while ISO/IEC 42001 is the certifiable management-system standard
The AI RMF does certify systems once Govern, Map, Measure and Manage are all documented
Certification exists, but only through an EU AI Act conformity assessment of the assistant
NIST certification is issued through AWS Artifact to customers who sign an addendum
questions.explanation: The NIST AI RMF is a voluntary, self-assessed framework that certifies nothing, whereas ISO/IEC 42001 is the standard an accredited third party certifies, and an EU AI Act conformity assessment is a market-obligation process rather than a NIST scheme.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A vendor serves a credit-scoring model over an API, with no weights, no training data and no gradients exposed. Which approach can still produce feature attributions for a single decision?
options: Decode the learned coefficients, which the API response returns with every prediction
Query the model with perturbed inputs and aggregate the changes with a model-agnostic SHAP explainer
Read the confusion matrix the vendor publishes, because it attributes each prediction to a feature
Compute gradients of the loss function, because the API returns them alongside the score
questions.explanation: SHAP offers model-agnostic approximations that only need repeated queries, so they work against a black-box endpoint, while the other three options all assume access to parameters, per-prediction attribution or gradients that the API never provides.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: During a guardrail test an answer is blocked and the team cannot tell which safeguard fired. What gives them the answer?
options: The CloudTrail event for the invocation, which lists the guardrail rule names
The model's response metadata, because the model names the rule it violated
The S3 invocation log, since every intervention is written there with its rule
The guardrail trace in the test response, which reports the interventions that occurred
questions.explanation: The trace reports which safeguards intervened on that call, while CloudTrail records who called which API rather than which rule fired, the model never sees the guardrail configuration, and invocation logging stores prompts and responses rather than the intervention detail.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A governance reviewer asks how ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is structured. Which statements are correct?
options: Its main body runs from clause 4 to clause 10 on a plan-do-check-act structure
Annex A holds the controls that support the AI risk and impact objectives
Certification is issued by an accredited third-party body rather than by AWS
It is a binding EU regulation that applies automatically to every deployer
It certifies an organization's management system rather than each application the organization ships
AWS publishes it as part of the EU AI Act package and refreshes it each year
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 42001 is an international management-system standard with clauses 4 to 10 on PDCA plus Annex A controls, certified by accredited third parties, and certification covers the management system rather than individual products; the binding EU instrument is the AI Act, which ISO does not publish.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: A team reads that Amazon Bedrock holds an ISO/IEC 42001 certification. Which statements about that certificate are correct?
options: It describes the certification of the AWS management system for the services named in its scope
Its named services include Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Q Business, Amazon Textract and Amazon Transcribe
The guide and the certificate can be retrieved from AWS Artifact
It transfers automatically to any workload a customer builds on those services
Customers remain responsible for assessing how their own use falls under the EU AI Act
It removes the customer's obligation to document their own model's intended use and limitations
questions.explanation: The certificate covers AWS's own management system for Bedrock, Q Business, Textract and Transcribe, is retrievable through AWS Artifact, and leaves the customer's EU AI Act assessment and their own model documentation untouched, because an AWS certification is not the customer's certification.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each responsible AI dimension to where it is demonstrated on AWS.
options: SHAP values, PDP and AI Service Cards
Guardrails PII filters, KMS and encryption
Policies, Model Cards and audit trails
Watermarking and disclosure that content is AI generated
questions.explanation: Explainability is demonstrated with SHAP values, PDP and AI Service Cards, transparency with disclosure and watermarking, governance with policies, Model Cards and audit trails, and privacy and security with PII filters, KMS and encryption.

questions.subdomain: 4.2 - Recognize the importance of transparent and explainable models
questions.question: Match each actor under the EU AI Act transparency rules to the duty that applies to it.
prompts: An assistant that chats directly with customers
The provider of a synthetic media model
A deployer publishing a deepfake video
options: Must mark outputs in a machine-readable format that can be detected
Must disclose that the content is artificially generated
Must inform people that they are interacting with an AI system
Must inform the natural persons exposed to its operation
questions.explanation: Providers carry the duty to tell people they are talking to an AI system and to mark synthetic output so it can be detected, while deployers must notify people exposed to emotion recognition and disclose deepfakes as artificially generated.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A benefits assistant retrieves the right sections of a policy document but occasionally adds a fee that never appears in the source. Which control most directly detects this at response time?
options: A content filter set to HIGH strength for categories such as violence and hate
A contextual grounding check that scores the response against the retrieved source and query and blocks below the threshold
A word filter using a managed list, which matches the invented fee as an exact string
A denied topic defined in natural language for the subject of fee waivers
questions.explanation: Contextual grounding checks evaluate the output against a grounding source and a query and return a grounding score, which is exactly the unfaithful-answer case. Content filters, word filters and denied topics target harmful content, exact strings and off-limits subjects rather than faithfulness to a source.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Before a fine-tuning job starts, a data engineer must find and classify customer PII and credentials sitting in the S3 buckets that feed the pipeline. Which AWS service is designed for that task?
options: Amazon Inspector, which assesses workloads for vulnerabilities and network exposure
AWS Trusted Advisor, which checks the account against best-practice recommendations
Amazon Macie, which discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3 using managed and custom identifiers
AWS Config, which evaluates resource configuration against rules over time
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie is the service for discovering and classifying sensitive data such as PII and credentials in S3, which must happen before any decision about how to protect it. Inspector finds software vulnerabilities, Trusted Advisor checks account-level recommendations, and Config evaluates configuration rather than object contents.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team is hardening a generative AI application ahead of a security review. Which controls are part of a defense-in-depth approach to securing it?
options: Encrypt prompts, artifacts and stored data with a KMS customer managed key
Record model invocations and guardrail interventions so an audit trail exists
Validate and filter model output before it is shown to the user
Depend only on the foundation model's own built-in safety training
Scope the invoking role's IAM policy to the specific models it is allowed to call
Publish the system prompt inside the client application bundle to make support easier
questions.explanation: Encryption, audit logging, output validation and least-privilege IAM are all named controls for securing AI systems, and no single one of them is sufficient alone. Relying only on the provider's safety tuning and exposing the system prompt are both single points of failure that a layered design rejects.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of a response to a suspected data-exposure incident in the order they occur.
options: Run a post-incident review and update the guardrails, runbooks and thresholds
Detect the anomalous activity through CloudTrail events and GuardDuty findings
Contain the incident by isolating the workload and revoking exposed credentials
Remediate the root cause by patching the vulnerability and tightening permissions
Restore service with enhanced monitoring while watching for recurrence
questions.explanation: Detection has to precede containment, containment has to precede eradication of the cause, and recovery follows only once the cause is closed. The post-incident review is deliberately last because it feeds the next round of controls.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Match each security capability to the purpose it serves.
options: Keeps traffic between your VPC and AWS services off the public internet
Caps the maximum permissions an IAM identity can ever receive
Applies content, topic, PII and grounding policies to model inputs and outputs
Discovers and classifies sensitive data such as PII stored in S3
Encrypts data at rest with a key you control and can audit in CloudTrail
questions.explanation: PrivateLink covers network isolation, Macie covers sensitive-data discovery, a permissions boundary caps IAM permissions, Guardrails applies policy to model traffic, and a customer managed key covers encryption at rest. Each capability sits at a different layer of the security model.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A regulated bank must call Amazon Bedrock from private subnets with no internet gateway, no NAT gateway and no public IP addresses. Which control meets the requirement?
options: A NAT gateway in each private subnet so traffic exits to the public endpoint
An interface VPC endpoint for bedrock-runtime through AWS PrivateLink
An IAM policy that denies calls made from outside the VPC
An Amazon CloudFront distribution placed in front of the model endpoint
questions.explanation: An interface VPC endpoint keeps Bedrock traffic on the AWS private network without an internet gateway, NAT device or public IP. A NAT gateway would still send traffic to a public endpoint.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A call-center summarizer must replace customer names and email addresses with placeholders in the model's output, and must refuse any response that contains a Social Security number. Which control implements this?
options: A word filter listing common first names and email domains
A content filter at HIGH strength for hate and violence
Amazon Macie scanning the bucket where summaries are stored
A Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information policy that anonymizes names and emails and blocks SSNs
questions.explanation: Guardrails sensitive-information policies act per entity type and direction, so names and emails can be anonymized while SSNs are blocked. Word and content filters do not target these entity categories.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team is securing an agent that can issue refunds and query customer records through tools. Which controls should it apply?
options: Grant the agent's role only the actions and resources each tool needs
Validate tool parameters and responses before acting on them
Require human approval before high-impact actions such as a refund
Log tool invocations and agent decisions for audit
Give the agent an administrator role so a tool call never fails
Let the agent follow any URL returned in a model response
questions.explanation: Agent security limits tool permissions, validates inputs and outputs, requires approval for high-impact actions, and records what the agent did. Broad roles and unchecked tool output turn a model error into an incident.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A platform team's pipeline role carries AmazonBedrockFullAccess, but policy now requires that the job may invoke only one approved foundation model. Which change meets the requirement with the least privilege?
options: Attach a customer-managed identity policy that allows bedrock:InvokeModel only on the approved model ARN
Add a permissions boundary that allows bedrock:* on all resources
Attach a service control policy that allows bedrock:InvokeModel across the organization
Turn on CloudTrail data events so any other model invocation is recorded
questions.explanation: Least privilege is expressed as a customer-managed policy scoped to one resource ARN. A permissions boundary and an SCP only cap maximum permissions and never narrow a request to a single model, while CloudTrail records calls after the fact.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A compliance rule states that fine-tuning data stored in S3 must use a key the company controls, with automatic rotation and a per-key audit trail. Which implementation satisfies the rule?
options: Server-side encryption with SSE-S3, because S3 already encrypts every object by default
SSE-KMS using a customer managed key attached to the bucket
TLS 1.2 on the S3 endpoint, because the rule is about protection in transit
An AWS managed KMS key shared with the account that runs training
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key gives you key policy control, automatic key rotation and per-key usage events in CloudTrail. SSE-S3 is the default with no customer key, TLS 1.2 covers data in transit only, and AWS managed keys are not customer controlled.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A bank runs inference through Amazon Bedrock and asks which item remains its own responsibility under the AWS shared responsibility model.
options: Patching the host operating system on the servers that run the model
Ensuring the Bedrock control plane is available in the chosen AWS Region
Applying guardrails, IAM permissions and encryption settings to the data it sends to Bedrock
Maintaining physical security of the data centers that host the service
questions.explanation: AWS secures the cloud (infrastructure, hosts, Regions, service operation) and the customer secures what is put into it: prompts, data, identities, encryption choices and guardrail configuration. The other three sit on the AWS side of the boundary.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A knowledge-base assistant sometimes follows instructions that were embedded in a retrieved document instead of answering the user's question. Which control most directly addresses this failure?
options: Increase top-k retrieval so the model has more passages to choose from
Add an output-side PII filter that blocks personal data in responses
Raise the model's temperature so responses vary more between runs
Attach a guardrail to the knowledge base that applies prompt-attack detection to user and retrieved content
questions.explanation: This is indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions arrive as data. Evaluating untrusted content, including retrieved passages, with a prompt-attack filter stops it before generation; retrieval size, temperature and output PII filtering never inspect instructions.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A community assistant must refuse abusive language, but users deliberately misspell offensive words so that an exact-match profanity list never triggers. Which control best meets the requirement?
options: Bedrock Guardrails content filters set to a high strength, which classify meaning rather than exact strings
A managed profanity word list, because it is free and covers common terms
Amazon Rekognition moderation labels, which detect abusive terms in generated text
A SageMaker Clarify bias report on the training dataset
questions.explanation: Content filters use classification across categories such as hate, insults, misconduct and violence, so spelling variants are still caught, and high strength blocks low-confidence detections. Word filters match exact strings only, Rekognition moderation covers images, and Clarify measures bias.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A security operations team wants an alert when an identity in an unfamiliar location removes a Bedrock guardrail or when model-invocation patterns look anomalous. Which service provides these findings?
options: Amazon Inspector, because it continuously scans workloads for vulnerabilities
AWS Trusted Advisor, because it recommends security best practices
Amazon GuardDuty with AI Protection, which raises findings for anomalous AI activity
AWS Artifact, because it stores the compliance evidence
questions.explanation: GuardDuty's AI Protection analyzes Bedrock, AgentCore and SageMaker activity and raises findings such as anomalous model invocation and guardrail removal. Inspector covers CVEs, Trusted Advisor recommends, and Artifact serves audit reports.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: An agent must call a third-party calendar API on behalf of signed-in users, reusing the access tokens those users already consented to. Which capability provides this?
options: Policy in AgentCore, which compiles plain-English rules into Cedar
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity, which handles OAuth flows and stores tokens in a vault
An IAM policy granting the agent permission to call the foundation model
Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information filters on the response
questions.explanation: AgentCore Identity supports machine-to-machine and user-delegated OAuth flows and keeps obtained tokens in a token vault so agents can act on behalf of users. Policy in AgentCore authorizes gateway tool calls, IAM authenticates AWS API calls, and Guardrails filter content.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team is adding hallucination controls to an assistant that answers questions about internal policy documents. Which measures belong in the design?
options: Retrieve passages from a Bedrock knowledge base and require citations in the answer
Run a contextual grounding check on the response and block answers below the threshold
Assign a confidence score to each response and route low-scoring answers to human review
Validate the response against the retrieved source text or an expected schema before release
Raise the sampling temperature so the model explores more possible wordings
Fine-tune the model so it memorizes the policies and no longer needs retrieval
questions.explanation: Exam objective 5.1.5 names RAG grounding, output validation and confidence scoring as hallucination detection methods, and all four correct options implement them. Raising temperature increases variance, and fine-tuning cannot keep a model faithful to documents that change.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A data engineering team is preparing customer records that will feed a fine-tuning pipeline. Which practices belong in its secure data engineering approach?
options: Data quality checks that catch schema violations, missing values and drift before ingestion
Row- and column-level access control so each job reads only the records it needs
Privacy-enhancing techniques such as tokenization or masking before records reach training
Integrity controls: versioned datasets, checksums and immutable audit records
One long-lived shared access key used by every stage of the pipeline
Keeping raw records unencrypted so engineers can debug failures faster
questions.explanation: Objective 5.1.3 pairs data quality, privacy-enhancing technologies, data access control and data integrity as the pillars of secure data engineering. A shared long-lived key breaks least privilege, and unencrypted raw data breaks data protection.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of enforcing a tool-access rule with Policy in AgentCore in the order they occur.
options: The AgentCore Gateway evaluates every tool call against the policy engine before the tool runs
The platform team describes the rule in plain English
The policy engine is associated with the AgentCore Gateway
The service converts the rule into a Cedar policy and validates it against the gateway schema
questions.explanation: Authoring starts in natural language, the service generates Cedar and validates it against the deployed gateway schema, the engine is attached to the gateway, and only then does the gateway evaluate each tool call before execution.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Place the stages of a response-validation pipeline for a grounded assistant in the order they occur.
options: The answer is scored against the source document and against the user's question
Relevant passages are retrieved from the knowledge base and inserted into the prompt
Responses below the confidence threshold are routed to a human reviewer
The foundation model generates an answer with citations to the retrieved passages
The validated answer is delivered and the interaction is written to the audit log
questions.explanation: Grounding must exist before generation, validation can only score a generated answer, and confidence-based routing happens after scoring and before delivery. Logging closes the loop so the interaction is auditable.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Match each security and privacy concern with the AWS feature that most directly addresses it:
prompts: Toxic content in a model response
Personal data in a model response
A CVE in a container image
options: GuardDuty AI Protection finding
Amazon Inspector scan
Bedrock Guardrails prompt-attack filter
Bedrock Guardrails content filter
Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information filter
questions.explanation: Each concern belongs to a different control family: prompt-attack detection stops instruction overrides, content filters classify harmful meaning, sensitive-information filters block or mask PII, GuardDuty alerts on anomalous activity, and Inspector finds vulnerable packages.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Match each documentation artifact with the question it answers:
options: Where did this dataset come from and how was it changed
What data assets exist and where are they stored
What are this model's intended uses, limits and results
What are AWS's own AI services' capabilities and limits
Who called which AWS API and when
questions.explanation: Lineage traces origins and transformations, a catalog lists available assets, a Model Card documents your own model, an AI Service Card documents AWS services, and CloudTrail supplies the who-and-when audit record.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A security reviewer asks which transport protection is required between the application and Amazon Bedrock. Which answer is correct?
options: TLS 1.2 is the minimum version for data in transit in the client and VPC paths
Traffic inside a VPC needs no transport encryption because it never leaves AWS
Encryption at rest with a KMS key replaces transport encryption
A dedicated AWS Site-to-Site VPN is mandatory before Bedrock can be called
questions.explanation: AWS states TLS 1.2 as the minimum in transit for these services, and encrypting data at rest answers a different question. Private networking helps, but it is not the documented minimum requirement.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A developer hard-codes the third-party API key used by an agent's action-group function in the deployment package, and the key is now visible in source control. Which change most directly addresses this?
options: Bake the key into an environment variable that is set when the function deploys
Encrypt the source repository with a KMS customer-managed key
Add the key to the function's IAM trust policy
Move the key to AWS Secrets Manager and read it at runtime with rotation enabled
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager keeps the value out of the code, retrieves it at runtime and rotates it on a schedule, closing both the exposure and the stale-credential problem. Environment variables still ship with the deployment, and neither a repository key nor a trust policy stores a secret safely.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team is applying privacy-enhancing technologies to the data behind its AI workloads. Which statements are correct?
options: Synthetic data lets a team test a pipeline without exposing real customer records
Differential privacy guarantees that the model will never produce a false statement
Tokenization replaces sensitive values with reversible placeholders that keep the record usable
Removing only the name field makes a record fully anonymous
Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so individual records cannot be isolated from aggregate results
Synthetic data removes the need for access controls and logging because no real records remain
questions.explanation: Differential privacy, synthetic data and tokenization each reduce exposure of real personal data while keeping analysis possible, and all three sit in the secure data engineering objectives. None of them stops a model from fabricating text, replaces access controls, or anonymizes a record on its own.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Place these checks in the order AWS evaluates them when deciding whether an application's request to invoke a model is allowed.
options: The organization's service control policy allows the action
The model's inference profile is active in the Region
The identity-based policy of the calling role allows the action
The resource-based policy on the target allows this principal
The permissions boundary attached to the role allows the action
questions.explanation: AWS evaluates the identity policy first, then the permissions boundary, then the organization's service control policy, and finally the resource policy, and a boundary or SCP can only narrow an existing grant. Region readiness is a service precondition rather than part of the permission evaluation.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A security standard requires a single policy statement that blocks unencrypted requests to a shared training-data bucket, even though other statements in the policies allow the read. Which statement meets the standard?
options: A Deny on s3 actions whose condition Bool aws:SecureTransport evaluates to false
An Allow on s3 actions whose condition Bool aws:SecureTransport evaluates to true
A Deny on s3 actions whose condition StringEquals s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is aws:kms
An Allow on s3 actions whose condition StringNotEquals aws:RequestedRegion is an unapproved Region
questions.explanation: A Deny conditioned on aws:SecureTransport false blocks every request that did not arrive over TLS regardless of any Allow, while an Allow is additive and can never take a permission away, and a server-side encryption header describes data at rest rather than transport.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team enables CloudTrail and then reports that none of the knowledge base Retrieve calls made by its assistant appear in the trail. What is the explanation?
options: Retrieve calls are management events, so they are recorded only for the first 24 hours after the trail is created
Retrieve is a data event: it must be opted into with advanced event selectors, and the recorded events are charged
CloudTrail never records knowledge base activity; only Bedrock model invocation logging can capture it
Retrieve calls appear only in the console event history, which keeps every event for a year
questions.explanation: Knowledge base Retrieve is classified as a data event, which stays off until advanced event selectors opt it in and is billed per event, whereas Converse and InvokeModel are management events recorded by default.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A Bedrock customization role trusts bedrock.amazonaws.com. The security review requires the standard protection that stops another account from causing the role to be assumed in this account. Which addition meets the requirement?
options: A StringEquals condition on aws:PrincipalOrgID so only accounts in the organization can trigger the role
A StringEquals condition on iam:PassedToService set to bedrock.amazonaws.com
A StringEquals condition on aws:SourceAccount set to the account that owns the job
A NotAction entry that removes bedrock:CreateModelCustomizationJob from the trust policy
questions.explanation: aws:SourceAccount in the trust policy pins the role to requests that originate from the owning account, which is the confused-deputy guard AWS recommends for Bedrock service roles; iam:PassedToService covers the different case where a caller passes a role to a service.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A junior engineer reports that SageMaker training jobs write to ML storage volumes with no KMS key configured, and concludes that the volumes are stored unencrypted. Which response is correct?
options: Correct: without a VolumeKmsKeyId the volume data is written in clear text and only the metadata is protected
Correct: the volumes must be encrypted by an account level default that the team has not switched on
Nearly correct: an AWS managed key encrypts the volume, so no key is visible but the key is shared across accounts
Not correct: a keyless volume is encrypted with a transient key that is discarded after encrypting, and VolumeKmsKeyId is only needed when a specific customer key must be used or audited
