questions.explanation: SageMaker ML storage volumes are encrypted even when no key is supplied, by a transient key that is thrown away once encryption is finished, so neither of the engineer's two claims holds.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team denies bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream on one model family, expecting applications that call Converse with that family to keep working. What happens?
options: The Converse calls are denied too, because Converse and ConverseStream are built on the two actions the statement denies
The Converse calls succeed, because Converse is a separate action that the deny statement never names
The Converse calls succeed as long as the response streams, because streaming follows a different control path
The deny has no effect, because a Deny on foundation-model resources cannot match an inference profile ARN
questions.explanation: Calling Converse requires bedrock:InvokeModel and calling ConverseStream requires bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream, so denying the two lower level actions blocks the higher level ones as well, which is why an organization wide block has to name the Converse actions too.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Two accounts must share a Bedrock guardrail and an S3 bucket of training data. Which statements about that setup are correct?
options: The caller identity policy and the resource policy on the shared resource must each contain an Allow, because both are required
An Allow in the caller identity policy alone is sufficient, because identity policies are evaluated before resource policies
KMS encrypted data crossing accounts needs a customer managed key the sharing account controls, because the default AWS managed key policy will not cooperate
The trust policy of a cross-account role must name the external account as a trusted principal
An SCP or a permissions boundary can supply the missing Allow when neither side has written one
A cross-account decrypt also needs a key policy or grant that permits the caller, in addition to the IAM permission
questions.explanation: Cross-account access needs an Allow on the identity side and on the resource side, a customer managed key for KMS, a trust policy naming the external account and a matching key policy or grant; SCPs and permissions boundaries only cap permissions, and evaluation order never makes one Allow enough.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of enforcing an approved Regions rule for AI APIs across the organization in the order the team carries them out.
options: An SCP denies the AI APIs when aws:RequestedRegion does not equal an approved Region
A documented exception allows aws:RequestedRegion set to unspecified for global cross-Region inference profiles
The team lists the AWS Regions the organization approves for AI workloads
The SCP is attached at the organization root or at the OU that covers every account
A test call to an AI API from a member account in a disallowed Region is attempted and confirmed to fail
The monthly cost report is reviewed to confirm that the policy reduced the bill
questions.explanation: The team decides the approved Regions first, then writes the deny on aws:RequestedRegion, records the exception that global cross-Region profiles need the value unspecified, attaches the SCP, and finally proves the block from a member account; a cost report does not test the control.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: A team must move an existing Bedrock workload off the public internet. Place the steps in the order the team performs them.
options: Private subnets are created in at least two Availability Zones for the workload
An S3 gateway endpoint is attached to the route tables with an endpoint policy scoped to the team buckets
Interface endpoints for the Bedrock APIs are created with a security group allowing inbound TCP 443
Routes are checked to confirm that traffic no longer points to a NAT gateway or an internet gateway
The application is repointed at the interface endpoint names and invocations succeed
A CloudFront distribution is added in front of the model so that responses are cached
questions.explanation: The private subnets come first, then the free S3 gateway endpoint, then the interface endpoints with 443 only inbound, then the application repointing, and only after that the check that no public route remains; CloudFront would carry the traffic back onto the public internet.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Match each policy control to where it attaches and what it does.
options: Caps what principals in an OU or account may do; grants nothing
Caps what a request to an organization resource may do; grants nothing
Grants the actions it lists to the IAM identity it is attached to
Grants the actions it lists to principals that reach the resource
questions.explanation: SCPs and RCPs only cap what an identity or an incoming request may do, whereas identity based and resource based policies are the two statement types that actually grant an action.

questions.subdomain: 5.1 - Explain methods to secure AI systems
questions.question: Match each asset to how its contents are protected at rest.
prompts: S3 Express One Zone SageMaker output
options: Encrypted with a transient key that is discarded after encrypting
Uses an AWS managed KMS key and the choice cannot be changed
SSE-S3 by default, with SSE-KMS available as the option
Uses AWS owned keys by default, with a customer managed key available
SSE-S3 only, because SSE-KMS is not supported
questions.explanation: Each asset has its own default and option: notebooks default to SSE-S3, keyless SageMaker volumes get a transient key, instance OS volumes are fixed to an AWS managed key, Bedrock custom models use AWS owned keys, and S3 Express One Zone output accepts only SSE-S3.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A compliance officer must obtain the independent third-party audit report for an AWS service before approving it for a regulated workload. Where is that report obtained?
options: AWS Config, from the configuration timeline recorded for the service
Amazon Inspector, from the vulnerability findings collected for the account
AWS Trusted Advisor, from the security checks in the support console
AWS Artifact, by downloading the agreement or audit report on demand
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service repository for AWS compliance agreements and third-party audit reports, which is where an officer proves what AWS itself is in scope for. Config records configuration state, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor surfaces account recommendations.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: An organization is standing up a governance program for its AI workloads. Which elements belong in that program?
options: A documented review cadence that schedules periodic reassessment of models and controls
Data retention and residency rules stating how long data is kept and where it is processed
A training requirement so builders understand the acceptable-use and safety policies
A single risk assessment performed at project kickoff with no scheduled follow-up
Continuous logging and monitoring so configuration and access changes remain observable
A practice in which each team interprets the shared policies in its own way
questions.explanation: A review cadence, data lifecycle rules covering retention and residency, team training and continuous monitoring are the governance-process elements the objectives name. A one-time assessment and per-team interpretation of policy both fail the definition of an ongoing governance process.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of a governance review for a new AI use case in the order they occur.
options: Approve the use case, assign named owners and set the next review date
Classify the use case and its data using the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix
Identify the applicable policies, regulations and required transparency disclosures
Collect evidence such as evaluation results, model cards and audit logs
Assess the risks and define the required controls, guardrails and monitoring
questions.explanation: Scoping decides which rules apply, the applicable obligations follow from that scope, and controls can only be designed once the risks are known. Evidence is gathered after the controls exist to show they operate, and approval with a scheduled review date closes the cycle.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each compliance service to the purpose it serves.
options: Records who called which API and when, giving the account an audit trail
Checks the account against AWS best-practice recommendations for security, cost and performance
Provides downloadable compliance reports and agreements for AWS services
Continuously scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure
Tracks resource configuration over time and evaluates it against rules
questions.explanation: Artifact supplies the audit reports, Config tracks configuration state, CloudTrail records API activity, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor reports account-level best-practice checks. Confusing Config with CloudTrail is the classic mix-up, because one answers what the state was and the other answers who changed it.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A European insurer must keep all inference processing inside the EU to satisfy its data residency policy. Which configuration meets that requirement?
options: A global cross-Region inference profile, which routes to low-latency Regions worldwide
Provisioned Throughput in us-east-1 with a CloudFront front end
A geographic cross-Region inference profile scoped to the EU geography
Any Region, because encryption at rest satisfies residency
questions.explanation: A geographic cross-Region inference profile keeps processing inside the chosen geography, which is the residency control. A global profile can route to any commercial Region.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A retailer is writing the data lifecycle policy for its AI workloads, which must cover customer deletion requests and regional rules. Which practices belong in that policy?
options: Maintain lineage that links each dataset to the models and indexes built from it
Set retention periods and delete data, including derived copies, when they expire
Verify deletion and keep evidence that auditors can review
Apply residency rules so data is stored and processed only in approved Regions
Keep every copy indefinitely in case a future model needs it
Rely on the model provider to delete fine-tuning data from all backups
questions.explanation: Lineage, retention and deletion, deletion evidence, and residency rules make the policy enforceable and auditable. Keeping copies indefinitely or relying on the provider defeats the policy.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the stages of the data lifecycle for an AI training dataset in the order they occur.
options: Delete the data when its retention period ends and verify the deletion
Classify the data and apply retention, residency and access rules
Collect the data from approved sources and record its lineage
Use the data for training, evaluation or retrieval
Monitor access and check for policy violations or drift
questions.explanation: Data is collected and its lineage recorded, classified with its rules, used, monitored, and finally deleted when retention ends.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: An auditor asks when a SageMaker endpoint stopped using a customer-managed KMS key. Which service keeps the configuration history needed to answer that?
options: AWS Config, which records resource configurations and evaluates them against rules over time
Amazon CloudTrail, which records who called which API
Amazon Inspector, which scans for software vulnerabilities
AWS Trusted Advisor, which recommends best practices
questions.explanation: Config stores point-in-time configuration and evaluates compliance over time, which is what answers when a resource changed state. CloudTrail answers who did what, Inspector covers CVEs, and Trusted Advisor recommends.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A team keeps discovering that the container image behind its inference service ships a dependency with a published CVE, and it learns this only after deployment. Which change best surfaces this earlier?
options: Enable Amazon Macie to classify sensitive data inside the image layers
Turn on Amazon Inspector continuous scanning for the ECR repository
Enable Bedrock model invocation logging for the inference endpoint
Add a Trusted Advisor service-limit check for the container registry
questions.explanation: Inspector continuously scans ECR images for package vulnerabilities and rescans when new CVEs are published, moving discovery earlier in the delivery cycle. Macie inspects S3 content, invocation logging records prompts and responses, and service-limit checks watch quotas.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A company built its own support assistant by calling a third-party foundation model through Amazon Bedrock APIs and augmenting prompts with its own knowledge base. Which scope does this use case fall into?
options: Scope 1 - a public consumer generative AI service
Scope 2 - an enterprise application with embedded generative AI features
Scope 3 - your own application built on a pre-trained third-party model
Scope 4 - a foundation model fine-tuned on your own data
questions.explanation: In the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, Scope 3 is your own application integrated with an existing third-party foundation model through an API, with no change to the model itself. No fine-tuning rules out Scope 4, and a self-built app is not a purchased app.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A regulator requires that prompts and model responses sent to the AI service are never stored and are never shared with model providers. Which configuration meets the requirement?
options: Set the retention mode to aws_review so the data stays available for AWS review
Enable model invocation logging so every prompt and response is archived
Use Global cross-Region inference so requests are processed in the cheapest Region
Set the Bedrock data retention mode to none so nothing is stored or shared
questions.explanation: Retention mode none is zero retention: nothing is stored and nothing is shared with a provider. aws_review deliberately keeps data inside the AWS boundary for up to 30 days, and invocation logging stores content by design.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: An AI governance lead wants reviews that catch problems introduced by model, prompt or data changes without waiting for the annual audit. Which approach best implements a review cadence?
options: An annual full review is sufficient because model behavior is stable between releases
Reviews run only after a production incident has occurred
A one-time review at initial launch, with no scheduled follow-up
Scheduled periodic reviews combined with an immediate review whenever a material change is deployed
questions.explanation: A review cadence sets regular scheduled reviews, and the review strategy adds event-triggered reviews for material changes such as a new model, prompt or dataset. Incident-only or annual-only cadences leave exactly the gap the question describes.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A small team wants one dashboard that flags unused resources, security-group exposure and account usage approaching service quotas. Which service is designed for this?
options: AWS Config, which evaluates configuration against rules you write
AWS Trusted Advisor, which runs best-practice checks across cost, security, performance, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence
Amazon Macie, which discovers sensitive data in S3
AWS CloudTrail, which logs API activity
questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor is the best-practice recommendation dashboard and its checks span exactly those categories. Config evaluates your own configuration rules, Macie finds sensitive data in S3, and CloudTrail records API calls.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A regulator asks an AI team to evidence how it trains its people and how it documents its AI systems for users. Which practices satisfy that request?
options: Role-based AI training with completion records for builders, reviewers and operators
Model Cards or equivalent records of intended use, limitations and evaluation results
Disclosure to end users when they are interacting with an AI system, where rules require it
A current inventory of AI systems with named owners and review dates
Relying on the model provider's public safety documentation as the team's own record
A single onboarding slide deck with no attendance or refresh record
questions.explanation: Team training requirements and transparency standards are evidenced by documented role-based training, published system documentation and user disclosure, all tied to an inventory with owners and review dates. A provider's documentation describes the provider, and an untracked deck is not evidence.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A team is reviewing its generative AI workload against the Security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Generative AI Lens. Which principles belong there?
options: Least privilege access across models, data stores, endpoints and agent workflows
Sanitizing user inputs and keeping prompts in a centralized, secured prompt catalog
Monitoring events through CloudTrail together with guardrails and response filters
Boundaries on agentic behavior so automation cannot exceed what the workflow needs
Choosing the lowest-cost model tier that meets the latency target
Automatically retraining the model whenever evaluation scores drift
questions.explanation: The lens security principles cover least privilege, securing data and prompt flows, monitoring and response filters, and controlling excessive agency in agentic workflows. Cost-tier selection and retraining decisions belong to other pillars of the lens.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A governance board wants controls that stop a non-compliant AI resource from being created rather than reporting it afterwards. Which are preventive?
options: An SCP denying AI APIs outside the approved AWS Regions
A Service Catalog product with template constraints on instance types
An Amazon Bedrock policy that pins a guardrail version across an organizational unit
An AWS Config rule that flags endpoints without encryption
An Amazon Inspector scan of container images after they are pushed
A Trusted Advisor check that reports security-group exposure
questions.explanation: SCPs, Service Catalog template constraints and Organizations Bedrock policies act before or at creation time, so they prevent the non-compliant resource from existing. Config, Inspector and Trusted Advisor detect conditions after resources are already running.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the EU AI Act obligations in the order they take effect.
options: Article 50 transparency duties for AI-generated content
Prohibited practices and AI-literacy duties
Annex III high-risk obligations
General-purpose AI model obligations and governance rules
Annex I high-risk obligations for regulated products
questions.explanation: The Act phases in over several years: prohibited practices and AI literacy first, then GPAI and governance rules, then Article 50 transparency, then the two high-risk tiers with Annex III ahead of Annex I.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of applying the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix to a new use case in the order they occur.
options: Prioritize the controls that each discipline needs for this scope, buying for Scopes 1-2 and building for Scopes 3-5
Re-scope and re-prioritize whenever the use case changes materially
Classify the use case into one of the five scopes based on ownership of the model and its data
Implement the prioritized controls
List the five security disciplines the classified workload must address, from governance and compliance to resilience
questions.explanation: AWS states the first step is determining the scope, which then fixes the buyer or builder perspective; the five disciplines are applied to that scope to prioritize controls, followed by implementation and periodic re-scoping when the use case changes.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of establishing an audit trail for AI interactions in the order they occur.
options: Enable CloudTrail management events so API activity such as model invocations is recorded
Decide what must be retained: who called which API, and the prompts and responses themselves
Apply encryption and a defined retention period to the log data
Review the logs on the agreed cadence for audits and investigations
Enable Bedrock model invocation logging with destinations in the same account and Region
questions.explanation: Requirements come first, CloudTrail then captures who did what by default, and model invocation logging (off by default) captures what was said with same-account and same-Region destinations. Retention and encryption follow, and scheduled review closes the loop.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each governance framework with its defining characteristic:
options: A binding regulation with risk-tiered obligations
An AWS mental model that classifies use cases into five scopes
A voluntary framework built on Govern, Map, Measure and Manage
A certifiable AI management-system standard
questions.explanation: The NIST AI RMF is voluntary and structured as Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, ISO/IEC 42001 is the certifiable management-system standard, the EU AI Act is binding law with risk tiers, and the Scoping Matrix is AWS's five-scope classifier.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each data governance strategy with the AWS mechanism that implements it:
options: Bedrock data retention mode set to none
S3 lifecycle rules and scheduled deletion
AWS Config compliance history and CloudWatch alarms
CloudTrail plus Bedrock model invocation logging
Choosing an AWS Region inside the required geography
questions.explanation: Lifecycle is handled by creation-to-deletion rules such as S3 lifecycle and scheduled deletion, logging by CloudTrail plus invocation logging, residency by Region choice, monitoring by Config and CloudWatch, and retention by an explicit data retention mode.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A healthcare company wants to process protected health information through Amazon Bedrock. Which statement is correct?
options: Bedrock is HIPAA certified, so the company only has to enable the service
The company signs a business associate agreement and uses only HIPAA-eligible services; no cloud provider is HIPAA certified
Turning on AWS Config rules makes the workload HIPAA compliant
HIPAA eligibility applies to the whole account rather than to individual services
questions.explanation: There is no HIPAA certification for any cloud provider; the correct construct is a business associate agreement plus HIPAA-eligible services. Config rules and account-wide claims do not create compliance.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A company deploys an application that falls under a practice the EU AI Act prohibits. Which statement matches the Act's penalty ceilings?
options: Up to EUR 35 million or 7 percent of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
Up to EUR 15 million or 3 percent of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
A flat EUR 7.5 million for every breach, regardless of company size
Up to EUR 35 million only, with no turnover-based alternative
questions.explanation: Prohibited practices carry the Act's top tier, up to EUR 35 million or 7 percent of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. The 15 million and 3 percent tier covers most other breaches, and the 7.5 million and 1 percent tier covers misleading information.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A European retailer is extending its generative AI assistant. Which statements about applying the GDPR to this workload are correct?
options: Transfers of personal data to another continent are prohibited outright
Individuals can request access to their personal data and, in defined cases, its erasure
Consent is the only lawful basis, so every other basis must be replaced
Processing personal data requires a lawful basis and a stated purpose
Prompts and model responses logged by the application can never contain personal data
The rules reach organizations that offer services to people in the EU even when processing happens elsewhere
questions.explanation: Lawfulness and purpose limitation, the rights of access and erasure, and the extraterritorial reach of the rules are the GDPR facts that shape an AI workload's design. Transfers are allowed with safeguards, prompts routinely carry personal data, and consent is one lawful basis among several.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: An auditor asks what the CloudTrail console can show about who invoked which models over the last quarter without any S3 trail configured. What is the accurate answer?
options: Every data event for the last 12 months, because the console keeps the complete record
The last 90 days of management events, which include the model invocation API calls recorded by default
The prompts and responses for the last 30 days, because they are part of the invocation record
Every event since the account was created, because event history is never expired
questions.explanation: Console event history retains 90 days of management events, which cover calls such as Converse and InvokeModel, while data events need selectors and prompt bodies need model invocation logging.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A team is asked which voluntary publication to start from when identifying generative AI risks inside a NIST AI RMF program. Which answer is right?
options: ISO/IEC 42001, because it is the generative AI profile that accompanies the NIST AI RMF
NIST AI 600-1, the Generative AI Profile that accompanies the AI RMF and describes 12 risks
NIST AI 100-1, because it is the generative AI profile and lists the 12 generative AI risks
The EU AI Act, because it is the voluntary NIST profile for generative AI workloads
questions.explanation: NIST AI 600-1 is the Generative AI Profile built on the AI RMF and it enumerates 12 risks, whereas AI 100-1 is the core Govern, Map, Measure and Manage framework, ISO/IEC 42001 is a certifiable management system standard, and the EU AI Act is binding law.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A security questionnaire asks which compliance programs Amazon Bedrock itself publishes as covered. Which answer matches the published set?
options: PCI DSS, FedRAMP, HIPAA and SOC 2, because payment card scope is always stated for Bedrock
FedRAMP and HIPAA only, because AWS publishes no international standards for this service
ISO, SOC, CSA STAR Level 2 and GDPR only, because AWS never states a US federal authorization for Bedrock
ISO, SOC, CSA STAR Level 2, GDPR, HIPAA eligibility and FedRAMP High in GovCloud (US-West); PCI DSS is not among the programs Bedrock states
questions.explanation: Those are the programs listed on Bedrock's own pages, and PCI DSS does not appear there, so the questionnaire must be answered from the AWS Services in Scope table rather than from an assumption.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A manager argues that because Amazon Bedrock appears in the AWS Services in Scope list for several programs, the team's workload is automatically compliant. Which correction is accurate?
options: The manager is right: scope status transfers to every workload built on the service
The manager is right, provided the team also turns on the AWS Config conformance packs
Scope status covers the AWS infrastructure controls; the team still has to implement and evidence the controls it owns for its data, IAM and configuration
The manager is wrong because the scope list has been retired and no service can be in scope any more
questions.explanation: AWS covers the infrastructure layer only, so an in-scope service still leaves the customer's own controls to build, evidence and report; a conformance pack can detect gaps but cannot transfer responsibility.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A US federal agency asks where it can run Amazon Bedrock under a FedRAMP High authorization. Which response is accurate?
options: Amazon Bedrock is FedRAMP High authorized in AWS GovCloud (US-West), and a per-model FedRAMP matrix is published for supported models
Every commercial AWS Region carries FedRAMP High automatically for every AWS service
FedRAMP applies to Amazon SageMaker AI only, because Bedrock is a serverless API
AWS holds no FedRAMP authorization, so the agency must assess the service on its own
questions.explanation: The published position is FedRAMP High in AWS GovCloud (US-West) plus a per-model FedRAMP matrix, and a deployment in a commercial Region does not inherit that authorization.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: A provider places a biometric identification system on the EU market as a high-risk AI system. Which obligations does the regulation impose on it?
options: Establish a risk management system that runs through the entire lifecycle of the system
Apply data and data governance measures to the datasets used for training, validation and testing
Keep technical documentation and give deployers clear information about how the system works
Design the system for human oversight, including the ability of a person to intervene or stop it
Publish the model weights so that any deployer can inspect the decision logic directly
Pass one conformity check at first release, after which logging and oversight duties no longer apply
questions.explanation: The requirements for high-risk systems cover a lifecycle risk management system, data governance, technical documentation and transparency to deployers, record-keeping, human oversight, and accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity; publishing weights is never required and the duties continue after market placement.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of retiring a production AI system in the order the team carries them out.
options: Personal and derived copies of the data are deleted or anonymized, and the deletion is verified
Named stakeholders approve the retirement and any legal retention periods are checked
Access to the retired resources is revoked and the AI inventory entry is closed
Traffic is drained and the endpoints, agents and knowledge bases are deactivated
The model, prompts, evaluation reports and approvals are archived for the record
A replacement model is deployed first, before any of the steps above are carried out
questions.explanation: Retirement starts with an approved decision and a check of retention periods, then traffic is drained and the resources deactivated, the documentation is archived, data copies are deleted and verified, and finally access is revoked and the inventory entry closed.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Place the steps of responding to a personal data breach under the GDPR in the order they occur.
options: Affected individuals are told about the breach when it is likely to result in a high risk to their rights
Security events are reviewed and it is established that a personal data breach has occurred
The breach record, covering facts, effects and remedial action, is completed and retained
The risk to the rights and freedoms of the affected individuals is assessed
The supervisory authority is notified without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours
The incident is held back until the next annual compliance report is due
questions.explanation: The controller first confirms that a breach happened, then assesses the risk to individuals, notifies the supervisory authority within 72 hours where feasible, tells affected people when the risk is high, and keeps a documented record of the facts, effects and remedial action.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each risk tier under the EU AI Act to a practice that falls into it.
options: Social scoring of individuals by a public authority
A chatbot that discloses that the person is talking to an AI
Spam filtering in an email client
A general-purpose model offered to downstream developers
Screening job applications or assessing creditworthiness
questions.explanation: Social scoring by a public authority is prohibited, CV screening and credit scoring are Annex III high-risk cases, a chatbot that admits it is an AI carries a transparency duty, spam filtering sits in the minimal tier, and a model offered to developers falls under the general-purpose AI rules.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each GDPR role to what that party does.
options: Determines the purposes and means of the processing
Processes personal data on behalf of the controller
Monitors how the rules are applied and can impose fines
The natural person whose personal data is being processed
questions.explanation: The data subject is the person the data is about, the controller decides why and how processing happens, the processor acts for the controller under a contract, and the supervisory authority oversees and enforces the rules.

questions.subdomain: 5.2 - Recognize governance and compliance regulations for AI systems
questions.question: Match each compliance program to what it covers.
options: Certifies an information security management system to a standard
Sets the controls for organizations that handle card payment data
Assesses cloud services for US federal agencies, up to High level
Reports controls for security, availability and confidentiality
questions.explanation: FedRAMP authorizes cloud services for US federal use at levels that include High, ISO/IEC 27001 certifies a management system, PCI DSS governs card payment data, and SOC 2 reports on a service organization's controls.
